items.statement: For a scheme S, M̃_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)(S) (so M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ) = M̃_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)/Pic_X) is canonically equivalent to the groupoid of tuples (L,L′,α,β,{x′(1)}_{x′∈Σ′∞}). Here L, L′ are line bundles on X′×S with deg(L′|X′×s)−deg(L|X′×s) = d for all geometric s; α: L→L′(R′), β: σ*L→L′(R′); and x′(1): S→Spec k(x′) for x′∈Σ′∞. The conditions are: (1) α|D−({x′(1)}) = 0 and α|ν^{-1}(Σ+)×S is an isomorphism; (2) β|D+({x′(1)}) = 0 and β|ν^{-1}(Σ−)×S is an isomorphism; (3) α|R′×S = β|R′×S, and Nm(α)−Nm(β), a section of Nm(L)^{-1}⊗Nm(L′), is nowhere vanishing along R×S; (4) (non-void only when Σ=R=∅) Nm(α)−Nm(β) is not identically zero on X×s for any geometric s. D± are the divisors of §5.3.2 (see coverage).
proofSteps: Translate the two parabolic flag conditions through Lemma5.12 and divide by the simultaneous Picard action.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Only a pointer ('the quotient description in Lemma 5.13'). It does not state the data or the four conditions, and Lemma 5.13 describes the Pic_X-torsor M̃_d(µΣ,µ′Σ), not its quotient.

items.name: Atkin–Lehner map on the comparison stack
items.statement: In the description of Lemma 5.13, AL_{M,∞}(L,L′,α,β,{x′(1)}) = (L(−Σ_{x∈Σ∞}µ_xΓ_{x′(1)}), L′(−Σ_{x∈Σ∞∩Σ+}µ_xΓ_{x′(1)} − Σ_{x∈Σ∞∩Σ−}µ_xΓ_{x′(d_x+1)}), α′, β′, {x′(2)}). Here α′ is induced by α using α|D− = 0, and β′ is induced by β using β|D+ = 0; on S′∞ this is x′(1)↦x′(2), i.e. Frobenius.
proofSteps: Apply the half-orbit formulas separately on L and L′, distinguishing Σ±.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Only a pointer; it does not give the formula.

items.name: Canonical identification of comparison stacks
items.statement: M_d(μΣ,μ′Σ)≅M_d×S′∞ by I=L^−1L′(R′−D−), J=σ*L^−1L′(R′−D+), with inverse provided by the root-norm Picard-stack exact sequence.
items.locator: §5.3.2, Proposition 5.15 (the isomorphism Ξ_M of (5.34)) and its proof, pp. 480–481. Part (1) of the proposition is the Frobenius compatibility, which is item 106.
proofSteps: Construct root-norm data from α,β and prove essential surjectivity/full faithfulness using (A.11), not a naive exact sequence of Picard groups.

items.name: Frobenius under the comparison identification
items.statement: Under Ξ_M: M_d×S′∞ ≅ M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ): (1) id_{M_d}×Fr_{S′∞} corresponds to AL_{M,∞}; (2) Ξ_M∘(Fr_{M_d}×id_{S′∞}) = (AL^{-1}_{M,∞}∘Fr_{M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)})∘Ξ_M.
proofSteps: Substitute the line twists from Lemma5.14 into I,J and compare the root sections.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: The item's first clause is Proposition 5.15(1), not a consequence of it; the locator names only (2).

items.name: Hecke grid equals signed incidence chain
items.statement: For λ∈{±1}^r, let H_λ := H_{λ1} ×_{→γ1,M_d,←γ2} H_{λ2} ×…×_{→γ_{r−1},M_d,←γr} H_{λr}, where H_{λi} = H+ if λi = 1 and H− if λi = −1, with projections γ_i: H_λ→M_d (i=0,…,r). For λ = µµ′ = (µ1µ′1,…,µrµ′r) there is a canonical isomorphism over S′∞, Ξ_H: H_{µµ′}×S′∞ ≅ Hk^{µ,µ′}_{M,d} (5.35), with p_{M,i}∘Ξ_H = Ξ_M∘(γ_i×id_{S′∞}) for i=0,…,r.
proofSteps: Off ramification use ordinary divisors. At ramification use (ϖ−a)β0=(−ϖ−a)β1 and β1=ϖγ+β0, yielding β0=−(ϖ+a)γ/2.
Characteristic two is excluded; a reduced-point calculation alone does not prove the functorial identity.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Vague ('identifies with the H_λ incidence chain'). It omits the definition of H_λ, the compatibility with all projections, and the base (S′∞). 'Including over nonreduced test schemes at ramification' is proof commentary.

items.name: Dimension of parabolic PGL2 bundles
items.statement: Bun_G(Σ) is smooth of dimension 3(g−1)+N.
proofSteps: Subtract the Picard-stack dimension from the rank-two bundle/flag stack.
items.note: Review note: Looks planned by GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.0, which constructs Bun_G with level structures and its deformation complex; smoothness and dimension 3(g−1)+N with Iwahori level at Σ follow there. That stage already owns item 27 (Iwahori parabolic bundles). Consider status planned [GS.0] if its blueprint states the dimension.

items.name: Dimension of the PGL2 Hecke grid
items.statement: Hk_G^r(Σ) is smooth of dimension 3(g−1)+N+2r.
proofSteps: Apply Proposition3.4.

items.name: Geometry of Bun_T
items.statement: Bun_T is smooth proper DM of dimension g′−g.
proofSteps: Use the Picard quotient/Prym comparison, retaining finite stabilizers.

items.name: Dimension of torus Hecke chains
items.statement: The torus Hecke stack is Bun_T×X′^r and is smooth proper DM of dimension g′−g+r.
proofSteps: Identify a line modification with tensoring by its signed point.

items.name: Geometry of H_d
items.statement: H_d(Σ)→Bun_G(Σ) has representable smooth projections of relative dimension 2d; H_d has dimension 2d+3(g−1)+N.
proofSteps: Use YZ17 Lemma6.8 and base change of the level structure.

items.name: Dimension of the comparison Hecke grid
items.statement: Hk_H,d^r(Σ) has dimension 2d+2r+3(g−1)+N.
proofSteps: Compute fibres of the bundle/divisor/leg projection by YZ17 Lemma6.10.

items.name: Smooth torus pullback
items.statement: If d≥2g′−1+N, M_d(μΣ,μ′Σ) is smooth separated DM of dimension m.
proofSteps: Apply Proposition5.15 and the geometry of M_d.

items.name: Proper Frobenius comparison fibre
items.statement: For an effective D on U=X−(Σ∪R), Sht_M,D^(μ,μ′) is proper over k.
proofSteps: Use proper Hecke projections and proper torus shtukas.

items.name: Octahedron compatibility contract
items.statement: (YZ17 Lemma A.9, Theorem A.10.) Given the commutative 3×3 diagram (A.10) of stacks over k with vertices A,B,C,D,U,V,X,Y,S and the stack N of (A.12), N ≅ (C×_Y D)×_{U×_S V}(A×_X B) ≅ (C×_U A)×_{Y×_S X}(D×_V B). Suppose: (1) A,C,D,U,V,X,Y,S are smooth and equidimensional over k; (2) U×_S V, Y×_S X, C×_Y D and C×_U A have the expected dimensions; (3) each of the squares (A.18) and (A.19) satisfies the conditions of §A.2.8 or the conditions of §A.2.10; (4) the squares (A.13) and (A.14) satisfy the conditions of §A.2.8. Then δ^!a^![B] = α^!d^![B] in Ch_n(N)_Q, where n = d_A+d_B+d_C+d_D−d_U−d_V−d_X−d_Y+d_S.
proofSteps: Identify the bounded derived tensor products on the common fibre product; compare support filtrations in coherent K0 with Chow by YZ17 PropositionA.5.
The finite flat presentations and enhancement are real hypotheses; the general intersection theory is not rebuilt in the shtuka roadmap.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Hypothesis (3) is too strong. YZ17 Theorem A.10 requires the squares (A.18), (A.19) to satisfy the conditions of §A.2.8 OR those of §A.2.10; only (A.13), (A.14) must satisfy §A.2.8. The item demands the finite-flat-presentation/regular-immersion (§A.2.8) conditions for all squares. As stated it would not apply here, because Proposition 5.18 verifies (5.20) through §A.2.10 (p. 487). Review note: Status 'planned [SF.5]' is not supported. SF.5 plans Fulton-style Chow groups and refined Gysin maps for schemes; it plans neither Chow groups of DM stacks with finite flat presentations nor the Octahedron Lemma. This is PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/34 (status missing), which that extraction routes to SF.5 as a source; that route has not been reviewed. Mark missing, citing YZ17/34 as owner, or planned only once that route is accepted, so that it is not owned twice. Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): status changed from planned (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5) to missing. SF.5 plans Fulton-style Chow groups and refined Gysin maps for schemes, not Chow groups of DM stacks with finite flat presentations or the Octahedron Lemma. The same statement is PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/34 (missing, source-routed to SF.5 by an unreviewed route); cite it as the owner. Routed to the SchemeAndStackFoundations source route.

items.name: Octahedron hypotheses for the ramified master diagram
items.statement: Let D be an effective divisor on U of degree d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}. Then (5.18) satisfies the hypotheses of the Octahedron Lemma (YZ17 Theorem A.10): (1) every vertex of (5.18) except Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ)×S′∞ is smooth and equidimensional (Proposition 5.17); (2) M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ), M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)^2, Sht^µ_T(µ∞·Σ′∞)×_{S′∞}Sht^{µ′}_T(µ′∞·Σ′∞) and Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞)×_{S′∞}Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞) are smooth of the expected dimensions; (3) (5.24) satisfies the conditions of YZ17 §A.2.8, and (5.20) satisfies those of YZ17 §A.2.10. For (5.24), Hk^{µ,µ′}_{M,d} is DM with a finite flat presentation, and θ^{µ,µ′}_{Hk} factors as a regular local immersion followed by a smooth relative-DM map. (4) (5.26) and (5.27) satisfy the conditions of YZ17 §A.2.8. In the proof of the regular-immersion step, the auxiliary Σ̃ ⊃ Σ must be chosen with deg Σ̃ > ρ, not ρ/2 as printed (E19).
proofSteps: Check each square against the exact YZ17 contract, using Proposition5.17 and finite flat presentations.
The conservative stronger auxiliary level is available after base extension; complete deformation-theoretic verification remains G3.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: The hypothesis is weakened to 'sufficiently large d', but the paper's bound d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g} is correct. The proof is not affected by E20, since Proposition 5.18 does not use Lemma 5.19. The statement also omits which conditions of Theorem A.10 are verified and how: (5.20) satisfies §A.2.10, not §A.2.8. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Σ̃ ⊂ |X−R| may be enlarged freely. With deg Σ̃ > ρ, the line bundle M = σ*L^{-1}⊗L(R′−Σ̃″) on X′ has degree ρ−deg Σ̃ < 0. Hence H^0(X, ν_*M) = H^0(X′, M) = 0, and since coker(e) injects into ν_*M, H^0(coker e) = 0, which gives the injectivity of the tangent map. Status missing; route 7.

items.name: Generic fundamental comparison cycle
items.statement: Assume d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g+min(N+,N−)}. The paper assumes the stronger d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g+N}; the weaker bound is implied by d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}. Let ζ♯ ∈ Ch_*(H_{µµ′}×S′∞) be the pullback of ζ = (θ^{µ,µ′}_{Hk})^![Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ)] under Ξ_H. Then over A♦_d, ζ♯ coincides with the fundamental class of H_{µµ′}×S′∞. In the proof, dim C_d ≤ m−1: apply Riemann–Roch to the factor X^{√R}_{d+ρ−N±−1} with N± = min(N+,N−). That factor maps to Pic^{√R;√R}_X with fibres of dimension d−N±−g, and the other factor is smooth of dimension d+ρ−N∓−1.
proofSteps: Use Riemann–Roch to bound common-zero degeneracy, then compare expected dimensions and the generic transverse locus.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Faithful to the paper. But Theorem 5.6 applies this lemma under d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}, which does not imply the lemma's 2g+N when g′=g and N≥1 (E20). The lemma's proof uses d ≥ 2g+N only to make one factor of the fibre product X^{√R}_{d+ρ−N−−1}×_{Pic^{√R;√R}}X^{√R}_{d+ρ−N+−1} an affine-space bundle by Riemann–Roch. That needs only d ≥ 2g+min(N+,N−), and this weaker bound follows from max{2g′−1+N, 2g}: if N=0 it is 2g, and if N±≥1 then 2g′−1+N ≥ 2g+N∓. The node should carry the weaker hypothesis so that item 121 holds at the paper's bound. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. This is the reviewer's repair for E20. The only step of the proof that uses 2g+N is the dimension count for C_d, and the count needs the affine-bundle property on one factor only. Status missing; route 7.

items.name: Cycle-intersection comparison
items.statement: Let D be an effective divisor on U of degree d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}. Then (Π_{x′∈Σ′∞} d_{x′})·I^{µ,µ′}(h_D) = ⟨ζ, Γ(Fr_{M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)})⟩_D. Here d_{x′} = [k(x′):k] and ζ = (θ^{µ,µ′}_{Hk})^![Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ)] ∈ Ch_m(Hk^{µ,µ′}_{M,d}) (5.42). The right side is ⟨ζ,Γ(Fr)⟩_D := deg of the D-component of (id,Fr_{M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)})^!ζ ∈ Ch_0(Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,d}).
proofSteps: Apply the octahedron identity on the determinant-D fibre and compare the torus-cycle intersection.
Use a conservative bound d≥max(2g′−1+N,2g+N,3g−2+N); the smaller printed bound is gated.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Replaces the paper's explicit bound with 'all largeness bounds imposed'. The theorem holds for d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}: its proof uses Proposition 5.18 and (5.46), not Lemma 5.19. It does not define ζ or the pairing.

items.name: Frobenius graph and cohomological trace
items.statement: Let S be a scheme over finite k, M smooth separated DM of pure dimension n, f:M→S proper, and C a self-correspondence over S with left projection representable proper. For ζ∈CH_n(C)_Q, its degree against the Frobenius graph over s∈S(k) is the trace of f!cl_C(ζ) composed with Frob_s on (f!Qℓ)_s.
proofSteps: Use cycle-class/Gysin compatibility and proper correspondence pushforward, with the fixed-point stack and the scheme base distinguished.
items.note: Review note: Statement matches YZ17 Proposition A.12 (= PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/35). Status 'planned [EDC.8]' is not supported: EDC.8 plans cohomological correspondences and trace classes, but explicitly leaves Frobenius point counting to the TraceFormula roadmap and the contracting/Fujiwara application to ET.5. YZ17/35 is missing and source-routed to EDC.8 by an unreviewed route. Mark missing, citing YZ17/35 as owner. Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): status changed from planned (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.8) to missing. EDC.8 plans cohomological correspondences and trace classes but leaves Frobenius point counting to the trace-formula roadmap. The same statement is PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/35 (YZ17 Proposition A.12; missing, source-routed to EDC.8 by an unreviewed route); cite it as the owner. Routed to the EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves source route.

items.name: Geometric trace formula for Heegner–Drinfeld intersections
items.statement: Let D be an effective divisor on U = X−Σ−R of degree d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}. Take Σ± = Σ±(µ,µ′), r+ = #{i : µi = µ′i}, r− = #{i : µi ≠ µ′i}. Then I^{µ,µ′}(h_D) = Σ_{a∈A♭_D(k)} Tr((f♭_{d,!}[H̄♦+])_a^{r+}∘(f♭_{d,!}[H̄♦−])_a^{r−}∘Fr_a, (Rf♭_{d,!}Q_ℓ)_a). Here H̄♦± is the closure of H±|_{A♦_d} in H±, with fundamental class [H̄♦±] ∈ H^BM_{2m}(H±) viewed as a cohomological self-correspondence of Q_ℓ on M_d; f♭_d = Ω∘f_d; and Fr_a is the geometric Frobenius at a.
proofSteps: Use the octahedron comparison, generic fundamental cycle, smallness to discard boundary corrections and the Frobenius-graph trace contract.
Impose the conservative bound recorded above until the printed low-genus endpoint is resolved.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Replaces the explicit bound with 'sufficiently large'. It also drops that the correspondences are the closures H̄♦± of H±|_{A♦_d}, pushed to A♭_d. The printed bound d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g} is valid once Lemma 5.19 carries its correct, weaker hypothesis (see item 118, E20).

items.name: Degree quadrangles
items.statement: Q_d is the set of four nonnegative integers (d11,d12,d21,d22) with d11+d22=d12+d21=d+ρ. Retain the shifted degrees d22−N− and d21−N+ when testing nonempty section moduli.
api: Project all four degrees and solve for d22,d21 from d11,d12.
Record admissibility/nonemptiness separately from membership in Q_d.
unitTests: Both diagonal sums equal d+ρ.
Membership in Q_d alone does not imply N_d is nonempty.
For d+ρ=0 all four unshifted degrees are zero.

items.name: Orbital comparison stack N_dquad
items.statement: Let d = (d11,d12,d21,d22) ∈ Q_d. Ñ_d = Ñ_d(Σ±) is the stack whose S-points are (L♮1, L♮2, L′♮1, L′♮2, ϕ, ψ_R). Here L♮i = (L_i, K_{i,R}, ι_i) and L′♮i = (L′i, K′_{i,R}, ι′i) ∈ Pic^{√R}_X(S), with deg(L′i|X×s)−deg(Lj|X×s) = dij for all geometric s; ϕ = (ϕij): L1⊕L2 → L′1⊕L′2 with ϕij: Lj→L′i; and ψ_R = (ψ_{ij,R}): K_{1,R}⊕K_{2,R} → K′_{1,R}⊕K′_{2,R} is O_{R×S}-linear. The conditions are: (0) ι′i∘ψ_{ij,R}^{⊗2} = ϕij|R×S∘ιj for all i,j; (1) ϕ22|Σ−×S = 0, and ϕ11|Σ+×S, ϕ22|Σ+×S are nowhere vanishing; (2) ϕ21|Σ+×S = 0, and ϕ12|Σ−×S, ϕ21|Σ−×S are nowhere vanishing; (3) det(ψ_R) = 0, and det(ϕ) vanishes only to first order along R×S; (4) (non-void only when Σ=R=∅) det(ϕ)|X×s ≢ 0 for every geometric s; (5) for each geometric s: if d11 < d22−N− then ϕ11|X×s ≠ 0, and if d11 ≥ d22−N− then ϕ22|X×s ≠ 0; if d12 < d21−N+ then ϕ12|X×s ≠ 0, and if d12 ≥ d21−N+ then ϕ21|X×s ≠ 0. Then N_d := Ñ_d/Pic^{√R}_X, for the simultaneous twisting action on all four L♮, and N_d := ⊔_{d∈Q_d} N_d.
api: Expose matrix entries, root maps, level constraints and simultaneous twisting.
Export the minimum-degree cutoff and both diagonal determinant products.
unitTests: Entrywise squares alone do not imply detψ_R=0.
At d11=d22−N−, condition(5) requires ϕ22≠0, not ϕ11≠0.
With all dij=0 and nonempty Σ−, condition(5) and vanishing force emptiness.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Conditions (1), (2) and (5) are given only as pointers ('the exact zero/nonzero level conditions in Definition 6.1', 'strict comparison on entry 11/12'). Condition (4) is omitted.

items.name: Root-section presentation and orbital map
items.statement: Map N_dquad to four root-section stacks of degrees d11,d22−N−,d12,d21−N+, with equality of their two tensor products INCLUDING the root section; g_dquad sends the matrix to Δ, a=ϕ11ϕ22, b=ϕ12ϕ21 and their common root ψ11ψ22=ψ12ψ21.
items.locator: §6.1.2, (6.2)–(6.3), pp. 493–494, and §6.1.3 (definition of g_d and g♭_d), p. 494. (6.4) is Proposition 6.2(3), and (6.5), (6.6) are in the proof of Proposition 6.2.
api: Expose the four entry maps and tensor-product compatibility.
Define g and g^flat=Ωg and compare with the geometric base A_d.
unitTests: The two root products agree because detψ_R=0.
Forgetting ψ_R prematurely loses the required tensor-product root equality.
a−b is detϕ, with exact order one at R.

items.name: Open presentation of N_dquad
items.statement: N_dquad embeds openly into the specified product of root-section stacks over the root-Picard-with-section stack. Geometric connectedness must be read with a nonempty/admissible qualification; arbitrary quadrangles can give the empty stack.
proofSteps: Translate conditions(1)–(5) into open restrictions in the section-stack presentation; separate nonemptiness from connectedness.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The nonemptiness qualification is needed (E22 confirmed): N_d = ∅ whenever d22 < N− or d21 < N+. Status missing; route 7.

items.name: Smooth orbital comparison stack
items.statement: If d≥4g−3+ρ+N=2g′−1+N, each nonempty N_dquad is smooth DM of dimension m=2d+ρ−N−g+1.
proofSteps: Use high-degree section maps in the larger member of each diagonal and the smooth locus of the rank-one root-matrix cone.
Prove the relevant image avoids the cone vertex using exact simple determinant vanishing.

items.name: Compatibility of the orbital tensor-product diagrams
items.statement: The square (6.4) commutes: ω_d∘g_d = (âdd^{√R}_{d11,d22−N−} × âdd^{√R}_{d12,d21−N+})∘j_d as maps N_d → X̂^{√R}_{d+ρ−N−} ×_{Pic^{√R;√R,d+ρ}_X} X̂^{√R}_{d+ρ−N+}. Here j_d is (6.3), ω_d is the open embedding (5.4), and âdd^{√R} is the addition of root divisors with sections (§A.1.4).
proofSteps: Identify each tensor product and its section from the same matrix products.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: There is a single square (6.4), not several diagrams. The maps are the root-divisor addition maps, not 'multiplication maps', and they are not named precisely.

items.name: Proper orbital comparison maps
items.statement: g_dquad and g_dquad^flat are proper.
proofSteps: Use proper addition/norm diagrams and the minimum-degree open condition as in the source; do not infer smallness.

items.name: Orbital coefficient local system
items.statement: Let L_Pic be the quadratic character local system of AppendixA. On N_dquad define L_dquad=j_d^*(Lhat_d11⊠Qℓ⊠Lhat_d12⊠Qℓ), equivalently the tensor of the characters on entries11 and12.
api: Construct pullback and expose its trace character η(L11)η(L12).
Record quadratic self-duality and compatibility with the tensor-product relations.
unitTests: The local system is rank one where defined.
Its tensor square is constant.
Its trace involves entries11 and12, not the determinant character alone.

items.name: Invariant injection of the rational base
items.statement: For effective D away from Σ∪R, inv:A_D^flat(k)→P1(F)−{1}, (Δ,a,b)↦b/a, is injective, with the endpoint conventions for a=0 or b=0.
items.locator: §6.2.2, p. 497 (the map inv_D; injectivity as in YZ17 §3.3.2)
proofSteps: Recover the section pair up to a common scalar from b/a and the prescribed divisor of a−b.

items.name: Orbital vanishing outside the Hitchin image
items.statement: If u is not in inv(A_D^flat(k)), the orbital term J(u,h_D^Σ±;s1,s2) vanishes.
proofSteps: An admissible adelic matrix configuration would determine exactly such a section pair and invariant.

items.name: Regular orbital trace identity
items.statement: For u=inv(a) not in {0,1,∞}, all d≥0 satisfy J(u,h_D^Σ±;s1,s2)=Σquad∈Q_d q^((2d12−d−ρ)s1+(2d11−d−ρ)s2)Tr(Frob_a,(Rg_dquad^flat!L_dquad)_a).
proofSteps: Identify the corrected root-divisor groupoid with the corresponding N_dquad fibre; apply weighted groupoid point counting.
All four entries are nonzero in the regular locus, so the minimum-degree rule introduces no cutoff.

items.name: Singular orbital trace identity
items.statement: Let D be an effective divisor on U of degree d ≥ 4g−3+ρ+N. If u ∈ {0,∞} and u = inv_D(a) for some (necessarily unique) a ∈ A♭_D(k), then J(u, h^{Σ±}_D, s1, s2) = Σ_{d∈Q_d} q^{(2d12−d−ρ)s1+(2d11−d−ρ)s2} Tr(Fr_a, (Rg♭_{d,!}L_d)_a). Here J(0,…) = J(1,…)+J(n+,…)+J(n−,…), and J(∞,…) is the analogous sum over w0, n+w0, n−w0. u = 0 lies in the image only if Σ− = ∅ (then a = a0 = (O_X(D+R),1,0)), and u = ∞ only if Σ+ = ∅.
proofSteps: Use the character-sum vanishing beyond the high-degree threshold to identify the finite minimum-degree cutoff with the regularized distribution.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: 'After the prescribed regularization' suggests an extra normalisation that the theorem does not make. J(u,…) for u ∈ {0,∞} is the sum (6.7) of the three orbital integrals, and (6.8) holds for it verbatim.

items.name: Root-divisor groupoid
items.statement: Div√R(X)=[A×/O×_√R], where O×_√R consists of local units with compatible square roots of residues at R. Its quotient by F× is the rational root-Picard groupoid. Keep the kernel stabilizers of O×_√R→O×.
api: Expose the forgetful divisor, degree, translation and Abel–Jacobi map.
Evaluate the quadratic idele character through the groupoid quotient.
unitTests: For R empty it recovers the usual divisor groupoid.
The local kernel at a ramification point is μ2.
Passing to isomorphism classes loses the 1/Aut weights needed by Lemma6.4.

items.name: Corrected orbital counting groupoid
items.statement: For γ̃∈GL2(F), X_(D,γ̃) is the simultaneous root-divisor quotient of (E1♮,E2♮,E′1♮,E′2♮,ψ_R), with integral induced ϕ, ψij²=ϕij|R, detψ_R=0, ϕ22|Σ−=0, ϕ21|Σ+=0 and divdetϕ=D+R. The determinant-zero root condition is absent from the printed list and is required.
api: Expose gauge fixing E′2♮=0, the root matrix and all three degree/character weights.
Prove the comparison with local Ξ_x counting before global summation.
unitTests: The all-ones residue matrix has eight admissible root matrices in odd characteristic.
Allowing all sixteen entrywise roots is a wrong definition.
Simultaneous translation leaves the two degree differences and η(E1♮−E2♮) unchanged.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. det ψ_R = 0 is required. The fibres of X̃_{D,γ̃} → Div^{√R}(X)^4 must match µ^{-1}(g) for h̃^{Σ±}_D = µ_*1_{Ξ_D} (6.11), and Ξ_x in §2.4.1 imposes det(α_ij) = 0 (Lemma 2.4). The bijection λ with N_{d,a}(k) needs it too (Definition 6.1(3)). E23 confirmed. Status missing; route 7.

items.name: Weighted groupoid orbital integral
items.statement: The orbital integral is ΣΛ 1/|AutΛ| times q^(-deg(E1−E2+E′1−E′2)s1)q^(-deg(−E1+E2+E′1−E′2)s2)η(E1♮−E2♮), summed over the corrected X_(D,γ̃).
proofSteps: Apply groupoid Fubini to the adelic torus action; normalized Haar-volume/image and finite-kernel factors multiply to one.
The root determinant condition matches exactly Lemma2.4.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. With det ψ_R = 0 added to X̃_{D,γ̃} (item 135), (6.9) follows from (6.10)–(6.15): (6.11) is checked place by place, at x∈R by Lemma 2.4, and the O^×_{√R}-descent constant vol(image)·#ker equals 1. Without the condition the formula is false: for ϕ = [[1,1],[1,1+ϖ]] at x∈R there are 16 entrywise root matrices but h̃^□_x(ϕ) = 8. Status missing; route 7.

items.name: Regular-fibre degree and character matching
items.statement: Under X_(D,γ̃)≅coproduct N_dquad,a(k), the two degree exponents become 2d12−d−ρ and 2d11−d−ρ, and η(E1♮−E2♮)=η(L11)η(L12).
proofSteps: Gauge-fix one root line, translate the four Hom degrees and use the quadratic tensor-product character law.

items.name: High-degree quadratic-character cancellation
items.statement: (Setting of §6.2.5: Σ− = ∅, D effective on U of degree d, a0 = (O_X(D+R),1,0) ∈ A♭_D(k), and d ∈ Q̂_d.) (1) If d12 ≥ 2g−1+ρ, then Σ_{Λ∈N̂+_{d,a0}(k)} η(L♮11)η(L♮12)/#Aut(Λ) = 0. (2) If d21−N+ ≥ 2g−1+ρ, then Σ_{Λ∈N̂−_{d,a0}(k)} η(L♮21)η(L♮22)/#Aut(Λ) = 0. Proof of (1): by (6.22) the sum factors, and its X^{√R}_{d12}(k)-factor vanishes because the fibres of AJ^{√R}_{d12}(k) all have the same cardinality q^{d12−g+1}−1 while η is nontrivial on Pic^{√R,d12}_X(k). (2) is the same with the N̂− analogue of (6.22).
proofSteps: Use AppendixA.6 exterior-power cohomology and the trace formula; identify the character on the stabilizer separately.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Vague and partly misdescribed. Lemma 6.5 concerns the weighted sums over N̂±_{d,a0}(k) with the character η on L♮ij, not 'a geometrically nontrivial quadratic L' (that is Lemma A.6). It bundles part (3), the identity orbit, which has a separate proof and should be its own item (see coverage).

items.name: Signed permutation representations
items.statement: Γ_d=(Z/2)^d⋊S_d. Let χ_i be the product of the first i signs, extend it trivially over S_i×S_(d−i), and set ρ_(d,i)=Ind_(Γ_d(i))^(Γ_d)χ̃_i for 0≤i≤d.
api: Expose induction subgroup, character and basis by i-subsets.
Compare the permutation module on the 2^d sign choices with ⊕iρ_(d,i).
unitTests: dimρ_(d,i)=choose(d,i).
Σi dimρ_(d,i)=2^d.
ρ_(d,0) is trivial, while ρ_(d,d) is the product-sign character.

items.name: Signed permutation module decomposition
items.statement: Ind_(S_d)^(Γ_d)(1)≅⊕i=0^dρ_(d,i), canonically by Boolean Fourier characters grouped by their support size.
proofSteps: Fourier-decompose functions on (Z/2)^d and group characters into S_d-orbits.

items.name: Ordered configuration cover and normalized IC sheaves
items.statement: Let X^◦_d ⊂ X_d be the locus of multiplicity-free divisors and X^{√R,◦}_d ⊂ X^√R_d, X′^◦_d ⊂ X′_d its preimages. Since X′ → X^√R_1 is finite étale of degree 2, ν^√R_d is finite étale over X^{√R,◦}_d, including divisors that meet R. The Γ_d-torsor (Γ_d = (Z/2)^d ⋊ S_d) is the ordered cover (X′)^d ×_{X^√R_d} X^{√R,◦}_d → X^{√R,◦}_d, which is the composite of the (Z/2)^d-torsor (X′)^d → (X^√R_1)^d and the S_d-torsor over the multiplicity-free locus. X′^◦_d is its quotient by S_d, a cover of degree 2^d that is not Galois with group Γ_d, and ν^◦_{d,*}Q̄_ℓ is the local system of Ind_{S_d}^{Γ_d}(1). L(ρ_{d,i}) is the local system on X^{√R,◦}_d attached to ρ_{d,i}. With j_d: X^{√R,◦}_d ↪ X̂^√R_d, K_{d,i} := j_{d,!*}(L(ρ_{d,i})[d])[−d] on X̂^√R_d; K_{d,i}[d], not K_{d,i}, is perverse.
api: Construct the ordered cover, its S_d quotient and associated local systems.
Expose the IC normalization and extend K_(d,i)=0 outside 0≤i≤d when indexing empty quadrangles.
unitTests: For d=2 the ordered cover has degree eight and the symmetric cover degree four.
The sum of local-system ranks is 2^d.
On a smooth d-dimensional open the unshifted K is a local system in degree zero, not perverse for d>0.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the target of j_d (the hat stack X̂^√R_d), the open X^{√R,◦}_d on which L(ρ_{d,i}) lives, and the fact the paper relies on that ν^√R_d is étale over X^{√R,◦}_d even where the divisor meets R (because X′ → X^√R_1 is étale). The E25/E26 corrections it makes are right.

items.name: Middle extension for geometric comparison
items.statement: For d≥2g′−1+N, Rf_d!Qℓ[m] is perverse and the intermediate extension of its restriction to every nonempty open of A_d.
proofSteps: Apply the small root-norm map and smoothness, checking the stated smallness bounds.

items.name: Geometric comparison decomposition
items.statement: Let d ≥ 2g′−1+N, A = d+ρ−N− and B = d+ρ−N+. Identify A_d with an open substack of X̂^√R_A ×_{Pic^{√R;√R,d+ρ}_X} X̂^√R_B by (5.4). Then there is a canonical isomorphism Rf_{d,!}Q̄_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{A} ⊕_{j=0}^{B} (K_{A,i} ⊠ K_{B,j})|_{A_d}. It comes from the Cartesian square (5.7), the Künneth formula and Rν̂^√R_{n,!}Q̄_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n} K_{n,i} for n = A, B.
proofSteps: Use the Cartesian root-norm presentation, the signed permutation decomposition and IC uniqueness.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the hypothesis d ≥ 2g′−1+N of Proposition 7.1. The item does not repeat the paper's remark that (2) holds for d ≥ 3g−2+N, and it should not: the proof given does not support that remark (see new issue on p. 507). It also omits the identification (5.4) under which the boxed products are restricted to A_d.

items.name: Positive incidence eigenvalues
items.statement: Suppose d ≥ 2g′−1+N, and let A = d+ρ−N−, B = d+ρ−N+. The endomorphism f_{d,!}[H♦_+] of Rf_{d,!}Q̄_ℓ preserves each summand (K_{A,i} ⊠ K_{B,j})|_{A_d} of (7.2) and acts on it by the scalar B − 2j = d+ρ−N+−2j.
proofSteps: Compute the sum of the B sign-flip operators on the generic Boolean cover, then extend by IC uniqueness.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the hypothesis d ≥ 2g′−1+N and does not name the operator (f_{d,!}[H♦_+] on Rf_{d,!}Q̄_ℓ, §5.1.5).

items.name: Negative incidence eigenvalues
items.statement: Suppose d ≥ 2g′−1+N, and let A = d+ρ−N−, B = d+ρ−N+. The endomorphism f_{d,!}[H♦_−] of Rf_{d,!}Q̄_ℓ preserves each summand (K_{A,i} ⊠ K_{B,j})|_{A_d} of (7.2) and acts on it by the scalar A − 2i = d+ρ−N−−2i.
proofSteps: Use the same sign-flip computation on the first factor.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the hypothesis d ≥ 2g′−1+N and does not name the operator (f_{d,!}[H♦_−] on Rf_{d,!}Q̄_ℓ, §5.1.5).

items.name: Middle extension for orbital comparison without smallness
items.statement: For d≥2g′−1+N, Rg_dquad!L_dquad[m] is perverse and IC from the generic open, although g_dquad is not small.
proofSteps: Use self-duality and show strictly negative boundary perverse degrees using character-sheaf cohomology vanishing and the boundary codimension.
Do not substitute a nonexistent smallness theorem for g.

items.name: Orbital comparison decomposition
items.statement: Let d ≥ 2g′−1+N, d = (d11,d12,d21,d22) ∈ Q_d, A = d+ρ−N− and B = d+ρ−N+. Then there is a canonical isomorphism Rg_{d,!}L_d ≅ (K_{A,d11} ⊠ K_{B,d12})|_{A_d}, with K_{n,i} := 0 for i > n. In that case N_d = ∅ (E22).
proofSteps: Identify the generic character local system and use the boundary middle-extension result.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the hypothesis d ≥ 2g′−1+N of Proposition 7.3. The out-of-range convention is right and matches E22.

items.name: Large-degree derivative–intersection comparison
items.statement: Let μ, μ′ ∈ T_{r,Σ}, with r± as in (5.13) and N± = deg Σ±(μ,μ′). For f ∈ H^{Σ∪R}_G put J^{μ,μ′}(f) = (∂/∂s1)^{r+}(∂/∂s2)^{r−}(q^{N+s1+N−s2} J(f_{Σ±}, s1, s2))|_{s1=s2=0}. If D is an effective divisor on U = X−Σ−R of degree d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g} (plus 2g+N if E20 is confirmed), then (−log q)^{−r} J^{μ,μ′}(h_D) = I^{μ,μ′}(h_D).
proofSteps: Differentiate the degree weights; the exponents are negatives of H± eigenvalues, giving (−logq)^r.
Apply Theorem5.6 and Theorem6.3 with the common conservative large-d bound.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: 'Sufficiently large' replaces the paper's explicit bound deg D = d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}. The statement also omits that μ, μ′ ∈ T_{r,Σ} and that N± = deg Σ±(μ,μ′). (Source issue E20 argues that the bound also needs 2g+N.)

items.name: High-degree spherical spanning modulo ideals
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero field E, a nonzero ideal I⊂H_x⊗E and any m>0, I+span_E{h_(mx),h_((m+1)x),…}=H_x⊗E.
proofSteps: Via Satake use t^n+t^−n, extend linear functionals invariantly to the finite inverse-image scheme in Gm, and use independence of n^a z^n.
Repeated Satake roots require the polynomial-exponential terms, not just evaluation at distinct points.
items.note: Review note: Statement matches YZ17 Lemma 9.1 (pp. 874–875). It is routed as a source to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5, but GZ.5's description (coherent theta kernels, the Waldspurger formula) does not plan it. This is a lemma about the spherical Hecke algebra H_x ≅ Q[h_x] and its Satake transform. It belongs with FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.6 (Hecke correspondences and the unramified Satake dictionary) or in this paper's Part II route.

items.name: Extension to the allowed Hecke algebra
items.statement: For μ, μ′ ∈ T_{r,Σ} and every f ∈ H^{Σ∪R}_G, (−log q)^{−r} J^{μ,μ′}(f) = I^{μ,μ′}(f). The paper states this for all of H^Σ_G, but J^{μ,μ′}(f) is defined only for f ∈ H^{Σ∪R}_G ((2.30); E28).
proofSteps: Repeat the finite-type image-algebra argument with the additional finite excluded set R.
Use high-degree replacements in products of local factors, not the invalid inference that a linear subspace containing algebra generators automatically contains their products.
Finish the separated-projector argument on this same algebra; gate G1 retains this proof obligation.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Phrased as an instruction ('must be proved…') rather than as a theorem. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The restricted identity is true and the argument sketched is complete. YZ17 Theorem 9.2 (pp. 875–876) goes through with H replaced by H^{Σ∪R}_G. (a) The image of H^{Σ∪R}_G ⊗ Q_ℓ in End(V′(ξ)) × End(A(K)⊗Q_ℓ) × Q_ℓ[Pic_X(k)]^{ιPic} is finite over H_y for any y ∉ Σ∪R: Proposition 3.39 holds for every y ∉ Σ, and §3.5.6 gives its V′ analogue. (b) Theorem 7.4 gives the identity on the span of the h_D, D effective on U of large degree. (c) The ideal generated by the h_y, y ∈ |U|−S, has finite-dimensional quotient. This is YZ17's Chebotarev argument on the Eisenstein curve, which tolerates excluding the finite set S ∪ R. (d) YZ17 Lemma 9.1 (item 149) at every x ∈ |U| gives surjectivity. Caveat for items 151–152: with this algebra, the idempotent e_π projects onto the H^{Σ∪R}-generalized eigenspace of m_π ∩ H^{Σ∪R}_G. That eigenspace equals Theorem 1.2's V′(ξ)_π (defined by m_π ⊂ H^Σ_G) only if no other non-Eisenstein point of Spec H̃^Σ_ℓ has the same restriction to H^{Σ∪R}_G. Strong multiplicity one separates only automorphic points, so this needs an extra argument (see E28).

items.name: Cuspidal spectral projector
items.statement: Fix ξ and put V′(ξ) = H^{2r}_c(Sht′^r_G(Σ;ξ)⊗k̄, Q_ℓ)(r). Let H̃^Σ_ℓ be the image of H^Σ_G ⊗ Q_ℓ in End_{Q_ℓ}(V′(ξ)) × End_{Q_ℓ}(A(K)⊗Q_ℓ) × Q_ℓ[Pic_X(k)]^{ιPic}. It is a finitely generated Q_ℓ-algebra of Krull dimension one (Corollary 3.40 and its V′ analogue). Y = Spec H̃^Σ_ℓ satisfies Y_red = Z_{Eis,Q_ℓ} ⊔ Y_0 with Y_0 a finite set of closed points (Theorem 3.41), and H̃^Σ_ℓ = H̃^Σ_{ℓ,Eis} × H̃^Σ_{ℓ,0} (7.8). Further, V′(ξ)⊗Q̄_ℓ = V′(ξ)_Eis ⊕ ⊕_{m∈Y_0(Q̄_ℓ)} V′(ξ)_m, where V′(ξ)_m is the generalized eigenspace. By strong multiplicity one, Π_Σ(Q̄_ℓ) ⊂ Y_0(Q̄_ℓ). For π ∈ Π_Σ(Q̄_ℓ), e_π ∈ H̃^Σ_{ℓ,0}⊗Q̄_ℓ is the idempotent of the point m_π; it acts on V′(ξ) as the projection onto V′(ξ)_π and on A(K)⊗Q̄_ℓ as the projection onto π^K. If the algebra is built from H^{Σ∪R}_G instead, e_π projects onto the H^{Σ∪R}-generalized eigenspace containing V′(ξ)_π. That eigenspace equals V′(ξ)_π only if no other point of Y_0 has the same restriction to H^{Σ∪R}_G.
api: Expose eπ, its action on cycles and annihilation of other spectral sectors.
Show the restricted-away-R algebra still separates the required cuspidal characters.
unitTests: eπ²=eπ.
eπ is zero on the Eisenstein factor.
Projecting two distinct cycles preserves μ and μ′; it does not replace their cross-pairing by a self-pairing.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Vague: it does not say which algebra e_π lives in, and it cites 'strong multiplicity one away from Σ∪R' without saying what this does and does not give. As printed (§7.2.1, §7.3.1), H̃^Σ_ℓ is built from H^Σ_G. If it is rebuilt from H^{Σ∪R}_G, as the repair of Theorem 7.5 requires, e_π projects onto a possibly larger generalized eigenspace.

items.name: Ramified higher Gross–Zagier mixed-derivative identity
items.statement: Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of G(A_F) = PGL_2(A_F), unramified outside Σ and, at each x ∈ Σ, an unramified twist of the Steinberg representation. Assume R ∩ Σ = ∅, and write Σ = Σ_f ⊔ Σ_∞ with Σ_f split and Σ_∞ inert in X′ ((1.4)–(1.5)). Let r ≥ 0 with r ≡ #Σ_∞ mod 2, let μ, μ′ ∈ T_{r,Σ}, let r± = #{1≤i≤r : μ_i = ±μ′_i}, and fix ξ. Then |ω_X| q^{ρ/2−N} ε−(π⊗η) / (2(−log q)^r L(π,Ad,1)) · L^{(r+,r−)}_{F′/F}(π) = (Z^μ_π(ξ), Z^{μ′}_π(ξ))_{Sht′^r_G(Σ;ξ)}. Here |ω_X| = q^{−(2g−2)} and N = deg Σ. ε−(π⊗η) = ∏_{x∈Σ−(μ,μ′)} ε(π_x⊗η_x, 1/2), with Σ−(μ,μ′) = {x ∈ Σ : μ_x ≠ μ′_x}. L^{(r+,r−)}_{F′/F}(π) = ∂_{s1}^{r+}∂_{s2}^{r−}[L(π, s1+s2+1/2) L(π⊗η, s1−s2+1/2)] at s1 = s2 = 0, with the normalized L-functions of §1.1.1. Z^μ_π(ξ) is the projection of the cycle class Z^μ(ξ) to V′(ξ)_π, m_π = ker λ_π ⊂ H^Σ_G, and the pairing is the cup product (1.3).
proofSteps: Apply the allowed-Hecke comparison to eπ, use the cuspidal spectral expansion and Proposition2.10, and divide by (−logq)^r.
This records the paper's endpoint; the repaired-domain and geometric-source proof obligations remain explicit gates.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: 'Under the full standing hypotheses' leaves the hypotheses and the objects implicit. Otherwise the identity, the constant C and ε− match (1.7). Review note: The proof (§7.3.1) applies Theorem 7.5 to e_π ∈ H̃^Σ_ℓ. With Theorem 7.5 available only on H^{Σ∪R}_G (E28, item 150), the argument gives (1.7) for the projection onto the H^{Σ∪R}-generalized eigenspace. See item 151 for what else is needed.

items.name: Boolean character projector
items.statement: For 0≤r1≤r, ε_r1=∏i=1^r1(1+σi)/2 ·∏j=r1+1^r(1−σj)/2 in Q[(Z/2)^r], acting through leg deck involutions.
api: Expose its Walsh expansion 2^−rΣI(−1)^|I∩{r1+1,…,r}|σI.
Prove idempotence, self-adjointness and the prescribed ± eigencharacter.
unitTests: For r=0 the empty product is one.
For r1=r it averages all deck transformations.
Starting the second product at j=r1 incorrectly gives zero when 0<r1≤r.

items.name: Product-of-derivatives identity
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.2, for 0 ≤ r1 ≤ r and μ ∈ T_{r,Σ}: |ω_X| q^{ρ/2−N} / (2(−log q)^r L(π,Ad,1)) · L^{(r1)}(π,1/2) L^{(r−r1)}(π⊗η,1/2) = (ε_{r1} Z^μ_π(ξ), ε_{r1} Z^μ_π(ξ))_{Sht′^r_G(Σ;ξ)}, with ε_{r1} as in item 153.
proofSteps: Change variables t1=s1+s2,t2=s1−s2; the Walsh expansion matches mixed derivatives with deck-translated cross-cycles.
Carry C through every line, then use self-adjoint idempotence. The printed proof drops C and overlaps the projector ranges.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: 'Fixed level parameters' should read 'μ ∈ T_{r,Σ}', under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.2.

items.name: Pushdown form of the derivative identity
items.statement: The pushdown Yπ^μ(ξ) to Sht_G^r(Σ;ξ) is independent of leg signs and has self-intersection 2^(r−1)|ωX|q^(ρ/2−N)ℒπ^(r)(1/2)ℒπη(1/2)/((−logq)^rL(π,Ad,1)).
proofSteps: For r1=r the projector is the deck-group average; apply push-pull for the degree-2^r leg cover.

items.name: Picard stack with square roots at R
items.statement: Pic_X^√R classifies (L,K_R,ι:K_R^⊗2≅L|R), graded by degL, with tensor product and all isomorphisms retained; no section of K_R is included yet.
api: Construct tensor products, inverse, unit and degree.
Expose the forgetful map to Pic_X and pullback under base extension.
unitTests: R=∅ recovers Pic_X.
At each geometric point of R, the forgetful fibre has μ2 stabilizer.
A square root is chosen as data, not just required to exist.

items.name: Root-Picard quotient and gerbe
items.statement: Pic_X^√R≅[Pic_(X,R)/[2]Res_R/kGm], where Pic_(X,R) rigidifies L along R and the action is through squaring; forgetting roots is a Res_R/kμ2-gerbe.
proofSteps: Trivialize the chosen roots locally and compare changes of trivialization; use fppf/étale descent with 2 invertible.

items.name: Root-Picard stack with a root section
items.statement: Pic_X^(√R;√R) adds α_R∈Γ(R×S,K_R) to root-Picard data; its associated-bundle quotient uses square action on the rigidification and weight-one dilation on α_R.
api: Forget α_R and multiply root sections under tensor product.
Export its associated Res A1-bundle presentation.
unitTests: The zero root section is allowed.
Scaling a root trivialization by u scales its square by u².
For R empty this extra datum is unique.

items.name: Root symmetric powers with sections
items.statement: For d ≥ 0, X̂^√R_d classifies tuples (L♮ = (L, K_R, ι) ∈ Pic^{√R,d}_X(S), a ∈ Γ(X×S, L), α_R ∈ Γ(R×S, K_R)) with ι(α_R^{⊗2}) = a|_{R×S}. X^√R_d ⊂ X̂^√R_d is the open substack where a is nonzero on X×{s} for every geometric point s (Definition A.2). For an open U ⊂ X, U^√R_d ⊂ X^√R_d is the preimage of U_d ⊂ X_d under ω^√R_d: X^√R_d → X_d (Definition A.3).
api: Expose root section, underlying effective divisor and Abel–Jacobi maps.
Restrict divisors to any open U and distinguish the hat space containing zero sections.
unitTests: R empty recovers the ordinary section/symmetric-power construction.
A zero global section lies only in the hat space.
A divisor meeting R has root stabilizer and is not an ordinary reduced scheme point.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Cites Definition A.3 but does not state it.

items.name: Root-stack fibre with nilpotents
items.statement: For one ramification point and a geometric scalar a(x), the root-forgetting fibre is SpecK when a(x)≠0; when a(x)=0 it is [Spec K[t]/(t²)/μ2], whose reduction is Bμ2. The nonreduced fibre must not be replaced by Bμ2 as a stack.
proofSteps: Base change the squaring map [A1/Gm]→[A1/Gm] along the chosen line and section; rigidifying its square leaves t²=a and residual μ2.
This is a root-stack fact reusable by the Bresciani24 root-stack source route.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Trivialize L_x and K_x. A point of the fibre over a(x) = 0 is then α ∈ O(S) with α² = 0, modulo Aut(K_x, ι) = μ_2 acting by α ↦ −α. So the fibre is [Spec K[t]/(t²)/μ_2]; equivalently, it is the fibre of [2] over the origin in the Cartesian square (A.1). For a(x) ≠ 0 the two roots ±α are exchanged by −1, so P_x = Spec K. The whole fibre over (L, a) is ∏_{x∈R(K)} P_x. The reduced fibre is Bμ_2, so coarse spaces, groupoid point counts and étale cohomology are as the paper uses them (E33).

items.name: Evaluation pullback and root symmetric-power smoothness
items.statement: Evaluating sections along R gives ev^R_d: X̂_d → [Res_{R/k}A^1/Res_{R/k}G_m], and X̂^√R_d = X̂_d ×_{ev^R_d, [Res A^1/Res G_m], [2]} [Res A^1/Res G_m] (Cartesian square (A.1)), where [2] squares both A^1 and G_m. Lemma A.4: (1) ev^R_d|_{X_d} is smooth; (2) X^√R_d is a smooth DM stack over k. Proof: over k̄, ev^R_d is the product of the ev_x: X_d → [A^1/G_m], x ∈ R(k̄). The incidence divisors D_x = {D ∋ x} satisfy D_I = ∩_{x∈I} D_x ≅ X_{d−#I} (via D ↦ D + Σ_{x∈I} x), which is smooth of codimension #I (empty if #I > d). So the D_x are smooth and meet transversally, and the smoothness criterion in the proof of Lemma A.4 applies. (2) follows by base change along (A.1); the stack is DM because [2] is relatively DM and X_d is a scheme.
proofSteps: Use local symmetric-polynomial coordinates to prove transverse incidence divisors, then the tame root-stack local model.
A zero-dimensional fibre may be nonreduced even though the total root stack is smooth.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Does not state Lemma A.4(1) (ev^R_d is smooth on X_d). It also leaves the Cartesian square (A.1) informal, and locates Lemma A.4 in §A.1.4, which is the addition map.

items.name: Addition of root divisors
items.statement: For d1, d2 ≥ 0, the rule (L♮_1, a_1, α_{R,1}), (L♮_2, a_2, α_{R,2}) ↦ (L♮_1⊗L♮_2, a_1⊗a_2, α_{R,1}⊗α_{R,2}) defines âdd^√R_{d1,d2}: X̂^√R_{d1} × X̂^√R_{d2} → X̂^√R_{d1+d2}. It restricts to add^√R_{d1,d2}: X^√R_{d1} × X^√R_{d2} → X^√R_{d1+d2} (A.2). Iterating gives p^√R_d: (X^√R_1)^d → X^√R_d (A.3), which is S_d-invariant for the permutation action.
api: Expose addition, unit, associativity and S_d symmetry.
Distinguish proper/quasifinite tame stack maps from representable finite maps when stabilizer kernels occur.
unitTests: Adding the zero divisor is the identity.
Multiplying root sections squares to the product global section.
At a collision in R, μ2^d→μ2 is multiplication and has nontrivial kernel for d>1.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Wrong locator (the addition map is §A.1.4; §A.1.5 is the Abel–Jacobi map). The statement also omits the S_d-invariance of p_d, which §A.2.1 uses.

items.name: Adelic root-Picard groupoid
items.statement: For x ∈ R put O_{√x} = O_x ×_{k(x)} k(x) and O^×_{√x} = O^×_x ×_{k(x)^×} k(x)^×, where the second projections are the squaring maps. Put O^×_{√R} = ∏_{x∈R} O^×_{√x} × ∏_{x∈|X−R|} O^×_x, which maps to A^×_F through O^×; the kernel is ∏_{x∈R}{(1, ±1)}. There is a canonical isomorphism of Picard groupoids F^×\A^×_F/O^×_{√R} ≅ Pic^√R_X(k), where the left side is the quotient groupoid of A^×_F by F^× × O^×_{√R}. It sends ϖ_x^{−1}, for x ∈ |X−R|, to O_X(x)♮ = (O_X(x), O_R, 1).
proofSteps: Choose a rational trivialization of L and local integral trivializations, then record square roots of the transition units at R.
Descend morphisms as well as objects; the quotient is not merely a set of double cosets.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the normalization of the equivalence (ϖ_x^{−1} ↦ O_X(x)♮ for x ∈ |X−R|), the definition of O^×_{√x}, and the fact that the isomorphism is one of Picard groupoids.

items.name: Symmetric-power rank-one local systems
items.statement: For a rank-one ℓ-adic local system L on the root curve X_1^√R, let L_d=(p_d!L^⊠d)^(S_d). Keep ordinary cohomological degree separate from perverse shift by d. The later extension to the hat section space is constructed by pulling back L_Pic, not by simply assuming an IC extension there.
api: Construct the S_d-invariant pushforward and its restriction to distinct divisors.
Export permutation/Koszul conventions and the perverse normalization.
unitTests: L_0 is the coefficient line.
For d=1 recover L.
L_d[d] is perverse on the smooth d-dimensional root symmetric power; L_d itself need not be.

items.name: Exterior-power cohomology of root symmetric powers
items.statement: If L is geometrically nontrivial, H^i(X_d^√R⊗kbar,L_d)=0 for i≠d, and H^d≅∧^dH^1(X_1^√R⊗kbar,L), Frobenius-equivariantly.
proofSteps: Apply Künneth and S_d invariants with the sign from odd cohomological degree; nontriviality kills H0 and H2.
The dimension bound is 2g−2 plus the actual nontrivial local conductor count, at most ρ.

items.name: Rank-one descent across collisions
items.statement: L_d is a rank-one local system on X_d^√R, including collisions at R, since the stabilizer kernel of μ2^d→μ2 acts trivially on L^⊠d.
proofSteps: Check the local tame stack quotient and the permutation action on the tensor line.

items.name: Multiplicativity of symmetric local systems
items.statement: There are canonical addition pullback isomorphisms add*L_(d1+d2)≅L_d1⊠L_d2, associative and commutative. For a general rank-one L its monodromy character takes values in Qℓbar×, not necessarily {±1}; only the ramification inertia is restricted to order two.
proofSteps: Define the tensor character on the distinct-divisor locus and extend by local-system descent; verify the coherence diagrams.

items.name: High-degree ramified Abel–Jacobi descent
items.statement: For d≥ρ+max(2g−1,1), L_d descends uniquely along AJ_d^√R to a rank-one local system on Pic_X^(√R,d).
proofSteps: Describe Abel–Jacobi fibres as the relevant weighted-projective/punctured-affine quotients, prove their geometric simple connectedness, and use effective local-system descent.

items.name: Character local system on all root-Picard degrees
items.statement: Extend the high-degree descended local system to all integer degrees by translating with large effective divisors away from R and tensoring with the inverse of their fibre; prove independence of this auxiliary divisor.
api: Expose translation comparison and its cocycle law.
Define the degree-zero unit fibre without choosing a degree-one rational point.
unitTests: Two successive translations agree with translation by their sum.
Changing the auxiliary divisor gives canonically isomorphic descent.
Negative Picard degrees are included even though negative symmetric powers are not.

items.name: Abel–Jacobi pullback in every nonnegative degree
items.statement: For every d≥0, AJ_d^*L_Pic≅L_d, including degrees below the initial descent threshold.
proofSteps: Translate to high degree and use multiplicativity to cancel the auxiliary fibre.

items.name: Unit for the root-Picard character sheaf
items.statement: There is a canonical trivialization ι: L^Pic|_e ≅ Q̄_ℓ at the origin e = O_X♮ of Pic^√R_X. For an effective D = Σ n_x x ∈ Div(X−R) of large degree d, L^Pic|_e ≅ L^Pic_d|_{O(D)♮} ⊗ L_D^{⊗−1} ≅ L_d|_D ⊗ L_D^{⊗−1}, and L_d|_D ≅ ⊗_x L_x^{⊗n_x} = L_D. The resulting ι_D does not depend on D.
proofSteps: Normalize the zero-divisor fibre and descend the high-degree comparison.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Wrong number: this is Proposition A.11(1), not a lemma. The statement is also vague ('the unit trivialization required by the multiplicative structure') and does not give the construction.

items.name: Multiplication and coherence of the character sheaf
items.statement: There is μ:mult*L_Pic≅L_Pic⊠L_Pic, with associativity, commutativity and unit coherence. Descend from the PRODUCT AJ_d1×AJ_d2, not a one-factor AJ_(d1+d2) with the wrong target.
proofSteps: Use faithful Abel–Jacobi descent on each factor, extend to arbitrary degrees by translation, and verify coherence after pulling back to three sufficiently large symmetric powers.
The source leaves these verifications as an exercise; they remain explicit construction obligations.

items.name: Ramified norm on root Picard stacks
items.statement: Let σ be the involution of X′/X and R′ ⊂ X′ the reduced preimage of R (ν: R′ ≅ R). Since r_R∘Nm = (r_{R′})² on ν_*G_{m,X′}, the pair (Nm, r_{R′}) defines a surjective homomorphism of étale sheaves Nm^√R_{X′/X}: ν_*G_{m,X′} → G^√R_{m,X}. It induces Nm^√R_{X′/X}: Pic_{X′} → Pic^√R_X lifting Nm_{X′/X}, namely L′ ↦ (Nm L′, L′|_{R′}, ι), with ι: (L′|_{R′})^{⊗2} ≅ (L′⊗σ^*L′)|_{R′} ≅ Nm(L′)|_R. Likewise (A.10) ν̂^√R_d: X̂′_d → X̂^√R_d, (L′, a′) ↦ (Nm L′, L′|_{R′}, ι, Nm a′, a′|_{R′}) lifts ν̂_d and satisfies ÂJ^√R_d ∘ ν̂^√R_d = Nm^√R_{X′/X} ∘ ÂJ′_d.
api: Expose the ramified fibre-root identification and tensor compatibility.
Compare root norm with the ordinary norm after forgetting roots.
unitTests: At a ramification point Nm(L)|x≅L|x′^⊗2.
Norm of the trivial line with unit section is the unit.
The ordinary norm alone forgets the datum needed to compare α and β at R′.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: The locator misplaces (A.10), which is in §A.3.2. The statement omits the sheaf-level construction (r_R∘Nm = r_{R′}², surjectivity) and the compatibility of (A.10) with the Abel–Jacobi maps.

items.name: Root norm exact sequence
items.statement: On the étale site, the root multiplicative sheaf gives 1→Gm→ν*Gm→ν*Gm→Gm^√R→1 with middle 1−σ and final root norm. The corresponding Picard-stack sequence (A.11) is exact in its 2-categorical sense.
proofSteps: Check local split/unramified/ramified norm kernels with 2 invertible, then pass to torsors with connecting automorphism data.
Do not read (A.11) as injectivity of Pic(X)→Pic(X′) on isomorphism classes; étale double covers can have a nontrivial pullback kernel.

items.name: Trace realizes the quadratic idele character
items.statement: For the quadratic anti-invariant local system of ν, the Frobenius trace function of L_Pic under the adelic root-Picard equivalence is η_(F′/F).
proofSteps: Check uniformizers away from R via the two lifts and cyclic Frobenius action, then use the multiplicative character-sheaf structure and adelic generators.

items.name: Serre quotient modulo constructibles
items.statement: For an essentially small finite-length abelian category C, construct Ind(C)/C with C embedded by Yoneda as a Serre subcategory; mc-isomorphisms become isomorphisms and mc-zero morphisms become zero. Apply to constructible perverse sheaves only after the finite-length and universe hypotheses are proved.
items.locator: Definition 3.32 and §3.5.4, pp. 445, 448 (extraction supplement: the paper works with the mc-notions directly and constructs no quotient category)
api: Expose the exact quotient functor and its universal property for exact functors killing C.
Transport actions commuting modulo constructibles into genuine actions in the quotient.
unitTests: Every original constructible object becomes zero.
A genuine ind-object with nonconstructible identity image need not become zero.
An mc-action satisfies its multiplication laws after applying the quotient.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound (supplement). C = Perv_c is essentially small and of finite length, so C is a Serre subcategory of the well-powered abelian category Ind(C) (see item 63), and the Gabriel quotient Ind(C)/C exists. A morphism becomes zero there iff its image lies in C, and invertible iff its kernel and cokernel lie in C. These are exactly mc-zero and mc-isomorphism, so mc-commutative squares and mc-actions become genuine ones. Routed to the EDC Part II extension, as the extraction proposes.

items.name: Zero-leg twisted shtukas and inner forms
items.statement: (r = 0.) Fix ξ: S_∞ → k̄, i.e. a k̄-point x^{(1)} over each x ∈ Σ_∞, and let Sht^∅_n(Σ;ξ) be the fibre of Sht^∅_n(Σ;Σ_∞) over ξ. Let B be the central simple F-algebra of dimension n² that is split outside Σ_∞ and has inv_x(B) = Σ_{1≤i≤d_x} c_x^{(i)} for x ∈ Σ_∞; it exists because Σ_{x∈Σ_∞}Σ_i c_x^{(i)} = 0 by (3.11). Let K_x ⊂ B^×(F_x) be a minimal parahoric subgroup for x ∈ Σ (an Iwahori subgroup of B^×(F_x) ≅ GL_n(F_x) for x ∈ Σ_f), and a maximal parahoric for x ∈ |X−Σ|, almost all coming from one integral model of B over X. Then Sht^∅_n(Σ;ξ)(k̄) ≅ B^×(F)\B^×(A_F)/∏_{x∈|X|} K_x as groupoids. The paper states this without proof.
proofSteps: Use descent of the Frobenius-periodic bundle to the indicated inner form and compare level structures.
Read the underlying classification source and split existence, equivalence and stabilizer conclusions (G3/G6).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Wrong locator: the r = 0 case is §3.2.2, not §3.2.3. The statement is vague ('balanced D∞', 'as in §3.2.3') and does not state the isomorphism, the algebra B or the level groups. Review note: Routed as a source to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands (GS.0–GS.3). GS.0 (adelic description of points) and GS.3 (with no legs, the cohomology is the cusp-form space) cover the split, untwisted case. The inner form B^× with parahoric level is not planned there.

items.name: One-leg Drinfeld-module comparison
items.statement: For r=1, μ=−1 and D∞=−Γ∞/n, the degree n(g−1)+1 component of the rank-n shtuka moduli gives the Drinfeld-module/elliptic-sheaf comparison stated in §3.2.3; after Pic^0(k) quotient it matches the PGL variant. This requires the exact Blum–Stuhler Theorem3.1.4 contract.
proofSteps: Match sign, degree component, infinity section and quotient with the elliptic-sheaf source; do not identify all degrees or all r with Drinfeld modules.
items.note: Review note: DrinfeldModulesAndTModules:DM.7 ('Prove the elliptic-sheaf equivalence in its normalized range') plans the comparison without level structure. The Iwahori level at Σ_f and the PGL_n quotient by Pic^0_X(k) go beyond DM.7 and remain missing.

items.name: Horocycle substack
items.statement: For κ0,…,κr with positive instability entries, κSht is the locally closed locus where every intermediate bundle is purely unstable with index κi.
api: Expose inclusion and each bundle-index constraint.
Compare under translations and restriction to coordinate supports.
unitTests: A chain with a semistable intermediate bundle is excluded.
An inadmissible adjacent pair makes the horocycle empty.
The stratum is closed inside its corresponding bounded open, not necessarily closed in the full shtuka stack.

items.name: Parabolic HN bounded open
items.statement: The truncation ≤κSht requires each intermediate bundle Ei† to lie in ≤κiBun_G(Σ); its horocycle is closed and the complement <κSht is open. This construction works before restricting κ to the admissible horocycle index set.
api: Expose inclusions for ordered bounds and open complement of the top stratum.
Prove cofinality using a nonempty family even when K_r is empty.
unitTests: Increasing every bound enlarges the open substack.
The top horocycle is closed in this truncation.
The finite-type case has a terminal sufficiently large bounded open, not an empty indexing family.

items.name: Necessary horocycle admissibility
items.statement: Nonempty κSht implies adjacent indices differ by one, Nr=N0, and Dr−FrD0 has exactly one geometric point over every infinity place and nowhere else.
proofSteps: Apply one-step Hecke adjacency and the terminal Frobenius half-divisor relation.

items.name: Horocycle support factorization
items.statement: For positive admissible κ, the leg projection on κSht factors through the coordinate subspace X(κ).
proofSteps: Stationary N forces a level-toggle leg; the final Frobenius relation fixes the infinity coordinates.

items.name: Nonempty signed torus shtukas
items.statement: Assume r ≡ #Σ∞ mod 2. (a) If Σ∞ ≠ ∅, then for every (μ, μ∞) ∈ {±1}^r × {±1}^{Σ∞} there is D′∞ ∈ 𝒟′∞ with D′∞ ≡ μ∞·Σ′∞ mod ν^*𝒟∞ and Σ_iμ_i = deg D′∞. One can take D′∞ = μ∞·Σ′∞ + m·ν^*x0(1) with x0 ∈ Σ∞ and m = (Σ_iμ_i − Σ_{x∈Σ∞}μ_x)/2 ∈ Z. Then Sht^μ_T(μ∞·Σ′∞) is non-empty: it is a Bun_T(k)-torsor over X′^r × S′∞ (Corollary 4.3). (b) If Σ∞ = ∅, such D′∞ exists iff Σ_iμ_i = 0. For every μ, define Sht^μ_T(μ∞·Σ′∞) by the Cartesian square (4.3), equivalently the T-shtuka stack of [YZ17, §5.4] base-changed as in §4.1.5. This agrees with Definition 4.4 whenever an admissible D′∞ exists, and it is a non-empty Bun_T(k)-torsor over X′^r × S′∞, because α^μ lands in the neutral component of Bun_T when Σμ_i ≡ #Σ∞ mod 2.
proofSteps: Change the divisor by pullbacks to adjust its degree in steps of two, then use the Lang-fibre description.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: The statement is false when Σ∞ = ∅, a case Theorems 1.2–1.3 allow. Then 𝒟′∞ = 0, so D′∞ = 0, and (4.1) forces Σμ_i = 0; for example r = 2, μ = (1,1) admits no D′∞. The proof step 'change the divisor by pullbacks' needs a place of Σ∞. Remark 4.5 inherits the same error (new issue).

items.name: Character local system on the hat section stack
items.statement: For each degree for which the root line-with-section stack is used, define Lhat_d as the pullback of L_Pic along its root Abel–Jacobi map. On the nonzero-section open it restricts to L_d by LemmaA.10. Zero-section stalks are supplied by this pullback, not discarded by extension by zero.
items.locator: §6.2.1, p. 497; L^Pic is constructed in §A.2.2, p. 521, and the restriction to L_d is Lemma A.10, p. 522 (the paper has no §A.2.3).
api: Expose the Abel–Jacobi pullback and restriction isomorphism.
Evaluate its stalk at a zero global section using the underlying root-Picard object.
unitTests: On the nonzero-section locus it recovers L_d.
The zero-section fibre is rank one, not zero.
For a geometrically trivial input its pullback is the corresponding constant/geometrically constant character local system.

items.name: The stack H_d(Σ) of injective maps of parabolic bundles
items.statement: H̃_d(Σ) classifies (E†, E′†, φ) with E†, E′† in Bun_2(Σ), deg E′ − deg E = d fibrewise, φ: E → E′ injective on each fibre, preserving the parabolic lines at x ∈ Σ, and an isomorphism on (Σ ⊔ R) × S; H_d(Σ) = H̃_d(Σ)/Pic_X for the simultaneous tensoring action.
proofSteps: Split out of the master-diagram construction (item 101) by cc-442dc5.

items.name: The Hecke stack Hk^μ_{H,d}(Σ)
items.statement: Let μ ∈ {±1}^r. H̃k^μ_{H,d}(Σ) is the moduli stack of ({E†_i}_{0≤i≤r}, {E′†_i}_{0≤i≤r}, {x_i}_{1≤i≤r}) together with a commutative diagram (5.17): an upper row E_0 → E_1 → ⋯ → E_r, a lower row E′_0 → ⋯ → E′_r, and vertical maps φ_i. The E_i, E′_i underlie points E†_i, E′†_i of Bun_2(Σ), both rows are objects of Hk^μ_2(Σ) with modifications at (x_i) ∈ X^r, and each (E†_i, E′†_i, φ_i) lies in H̃_d(Σ) (Definition 5.7). Hk^r_{H,d}(Σ) := H̃k^μ_{H,d}(Σ)/Pic_X, where Pic_X acts by simultaneous tensoring; it is canonically independent of μ. It carries column projections p_{H,i}: Hk^r_{H,d}(Σ) → H_d(Σ) and row projections ←→q: Hk^r_{H,d}(Σ) → Hk^r_G(Σ)². Finally, Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ) := Hk^r_{H,d}(Σ) ×_{X^r} X′^r.
proofSteps: Split out of the master-diagram construction (item 101) by cc-442dc5.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: Omits part (2) of Definition 5.8, the quotient Hk^r_{H,d}(Σ) := H̃k^μ_{H,d}(Σ)/Pic_X, which is canonically independent of μ and is the object used later. It also omits the projections p_{H,i} and ←→q and the base change Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ).

items.name: The torus pullback M_d(μΣ, μ′Σ)
items.statement: M_d(μ_Σ, μ′_Σ) := (Bun_T² × S′_∞) ×_{θ^{μ,μ′}_{Bun}, Bun_G(Σ)², ←→p_H} H_d(Σ), the fibre product of the bottom row of (5.18) (Cartesian square (5.23)). Here θ^{μ,μ′}_{Bun} = θ^{μ_Σ}_{Bun} × θ^{μ′_Σ}_{Bun}, using a common copy of S′_∞, so M_d(μ_Σ, μ′_Σ) depends only on μ_Σ and μ′_Σ. It carries the Atkin–Lehner automorphism AL_{M,∞}.
proofSteps: Split out of the master-diagram construction (item 101) by cc-442dc5.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: 'Pulling H_d(Σ) back along the two maps from Bun_T-type data' is imprecise. It is one fibre product, over Bun_G(Σ)², of θ^{μ,μ′}_{Bun} and ←→p_H.

items.name: The Hecke stack Hk^{μ,μ′}_{M,d}
items.statement: Hk^{μ,μ′}_{M,d} is the fibre product of the top row of (5.18).
proofSteps: Split out of the master-diagram construction (item 101) by cc-442dc5.

items.name: The Frobenius-intersection stack Sht^{μ,μ′}_{M,d}
items.statement: Sht^{μ,μ′}_{M,d} is the fibre product of the maps in (5.25), intersecting Hk^{μ,μ′}_{M,d} with the graph of Frobenius.
proofSteps: Split out of the master-diagram construction (item 101) by cc-442dc5.

items.name: Conjecture 1.6 (statement only)
items.statement: Conjecture 1.6 (statement only; not proved). Let ρ_π be the rank-two ℓ-adic local system attached to π by Drinfeld, with det ρ_π ≅ Q̄ℓ(−1). Put W′_π = H^1(X′⊗k̄, j′_{!*}ν^*ρ_π), so that L(π_{F′}, s−½) = det(1 − q^{−s}Fr | W′_π). Assume the expected identification V′(ξ)_π ≅ π^K ⊗ W′_π^{⊗r} ⊗ ℓ_{π,ξ} (a consequence of the expected (1.9); π^K and ℓ_{π,ξ} are lines). Let r = ord_{s=1/2}L(π_{F′},s), the dimension of the generalised q-eigenspace of Fr on W′_π, and let μ ∈ T_{r,Σ}. Then Z^μ_π(ξ) ∈ π^K ⊗ ∧^r(W′_π^{Fr=q}) ⊗ ℓ_{π,ξ}.
proofSteps: A conjecture the paper states; no proof is claimed.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19): statement corrected against the paper: The statement omits that the ambient identification V′(ξ)_π ≅ π^K ⊗ W′_π^{⊗r} ⊗ ℓ_{π,ξ} is only expected (it follows from the conjectural (1.9)). It also leaves W′_π undefined. 'W_{π′}' should read W′_π. The prerequisite is better given as items 78 (Theorem 1.1) and 86 (the cycles) than as 154.

items.name: Functional equation and root number of the two-variable L-function
items.statement: Let π be cuspidal on PGL2(A_F), unramified outside Σ and an unramified quadratic twist of Steinberg at each x ∈ Σ, with Σ ∩ R = ∅, N = deg Σ, ρ = deg R, and Σ = Σf ⊔ Σ∞ the split/inert decomposition. Then L(π,s) and L(π⊗η,s) are polynomials in q^{−s} of degrees 4g−4+N and 4g−4+2ρ+N. The root number of π_{F′} is (−1)^{#Σ∞}: each x ∈ Σf contributes +1, and each x ∈ Σ∞ contributes −1 because BC(π_x) is the Steinberg representation. Hence ℒ_{F′/F}(π,s1,s2) = (−1)^{#Σ∞}ℒ_{F′/F}(π,−s1,−s2), for both the §1.1.1 and the §2.6.1 normalisation. Consequently ℒ^{(r+,r−)}_{F′/F}(π) = 0 unless r+ + r− ≡ #Σ∞ mod 2.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The paper states and proves this (p.415), and it fixes the parity r ≡ #Σ∞ under which Theorems 1.2–1.3 and Conjecture 1.6 are non-vacuous. No item states it: item 12 only mentions even/odd, and item 13 only defines the function. Suggested owner: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.2 (generic global functional equation only) GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.2 (local ε-factors of St⊗χ) Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Level test functions J_x and the global test function f_{Σ±}
items.statement: Fix Σ = Σ+ ⊔ Σ−; later Σ± = Σ±(μ,μ′) of (4.5)–(4.6). Put N± = deg Σ±. For x ∈ Σ+, J_x = Iw_x = {g ∈ G(O_x): g ≡ [[*,*],[0,*]] mod m_x}. For x ∈ Σ−, J_x = Iw_x·w = {g ∈ G(O_x): g ≡ [[*,*],[*,0]] mod m_x}, with w = [[0,1],[−1,0]]. For f ∈ H^{Σ∪R}_G put f_{Σ±} = f ⊗ (⊗_{x∈R} h□_x) ⊗ (⊗_{x∈Σ} 1_{J_x}) ∈ C_c^∞(G(A)). Finally, ε−(π⊗η) := ∏_{x∈Σ−} ε(π_x⊗η_x,½), the product of the Atkin–Lehner eigenvalues of π⊗η at Σ−.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The global test function f_{Σ±} is used in Proposition 2.10, Theorem 6.3 and Theorem 7.4 (items 26, 131–133, 148, 150), but no item defines it or the local sets J_x. Suggested owner:  Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Global RTF equality of the h□ and f□ tests (repair)
items.statement: Let x0 ∈ R and let φ ∈ C_c^∞(G(F_{x0})) be either right A(O_{x0})-invariant or left A(O_{x0})-η_{x0}-eigen. Then for every f′ ∈ C_c^∞(G(A^{x0})) and every γ, J(φ⊗f′,s1,s2) = 0, J(γ,φ⊗f′,s1,s2) = 0 and J_π(φ⊗f′,s1,s2) = 0. For the global J, translate h2 (resp. h1) by t ∈ A(O_{x0}) with η_{x0}(t) = −1; the degree regularisation is A(O)-invariant. Let f^□_{Σ±} be f_{Σ±} with every h□_x (x ∈ R) replaced by f□_x. Then J(f_{Σ±}) = J(f^□_{Σ±}) by Lemma 2.6. If moreover f ∈ I^{Σ∪R}_Eis, then J(f_{Σ±},s1,s2) = Σ_π J_π(f_{Σ±},s1,s2), a finite sum over cuspidal π, by Lemma 2.3 for f^□_{Σ±} (f□_x is left GL2(O_x)-invariant) and Proposition 2.8.
items.locator: Repair of Theorem 2.2/Lemma 2.3, pp.404–405, via Lemma 2.6, pp.408–409; used at (7.10), p.513
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The spectral expansion J(f_{Σ±}) = Σ_π J_π(f_{Σ±}) that (7.10) uses does not follow from Lemma 2.3 as printed, because h□_x is not left Iw_x-invariant. The corrected argument needs its own node. Suggested owner:  Route: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights.

items.name: Torus shtukas as a base change of the YZ17 T-shtukas
items.statement: For (μ, μ∞) ∈ {±1}^r × {±1}^{Σ∞}, put μ̃ = (μ, −μ∞). Let Sht^{μ̃}_T → X′^r × X′^{Σ∞} be the T-shtuka stack of [YZ17, §5.4], defined with the Frobenius isomorphism in Bun_T = Pic_{X′}/Pic_X; it is also valid for ramified X′/X. Then Sht^μ_T(μ∞·Σ′∞) ≅ Sht^{μ̃}_T ×_{X′^r×X′^{Σ∞}} (X′^r × S′∞), where S′∞ → X′^{Σ∞} is the product of the embeddings Spec k(x′) ↪ X′ recording x′(1). When Σ∞ = ∅ the right side is Sht^μ_T of [YZ17] for every μ with r even.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The item is unnumbered but load-bearing. It ties the ramified torus shtukas to the YZ17 branch of the same Part II roadmap without duplication, and it is the correct definition when Σ∞ = ∅ and Σμ_i ≠ 0 (new issue on Remark 4.5). Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Non-vanishing of Heegner–Drinfeld classes in high rank
items.statement: Keep the hypotheses of Theorem 1.2. Let r ≡ #Σ∞ mod 2 with r ≥ ord_{s=1/2}L(π_{F′},s), and suppose L(π_{F′},s) is not constant, i.e. 4g−4+N+ρ > 0. Then Z^μ_π(ξ) ≠ 0 for all μ ∈ T_{r,Σ} and ξ ∈ S′∞(k̄). Proof: take μ′ = μ in Theorem 1.2, so r+ = r, r− = 0, Σ− = ∅ and ε− = 1. This gives (Z^μ_π(ξ),Z^μ_π(ξ)) = |ω_X|q^{ρ/2−N}ℒ^{(r)}(π_{F′},½)/(2(−log q)^r L(π,Ad,1)). By [YZ17, Th. B.2] ℒ^{(r)}(π_{F′},½) ≠ 0, since r ≥ ord and r ≡ ord mod 2 by the root number.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The paper states this consequence of Theorem 1.2 and YZ17 super-positivity (PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/37) with a proof sketch. It is the unconditional content behind Conjecture 1.6 (item 190). Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Unramified and Steinberg Whittaker newvectors and their local factors
items.statement: Let ψ_x be unramified and use measures with vol(O_x^×) = 1. (a) If π_x is unramified with Satake parameter diag(α,β), αβ = 1, the G(O_x)-fixed W0 with W0(1) = 1 has W0(diag(ϖ^n,1)) = q_x^{−n/2}(α^{n+1}−β^{n+1})/(α−β) for n ≥ 0 (as a polynomial in α, β) and 0 for n < 0. Also λ♮_x(W0,χ,s) = 1 for unramified χ, and θ♮_x(W0,W0) = 1 − q_x^{−2}. (b) If π_x = St⊗χ with χ unramified quadratic, the Iw_x-fixed W0 with W0(1) = 1 has W0(diag(a,1)) = χ(a)|a| for v(a) ≥ 0 and 0 otherwise. Its translate satisfies (π_x(w)W0)(diag(a,1)) = −q_x^{−1}χ(a)|a| for v(a) ≥ −1 and 0 for v(a) ≤ −2. Further θ♮_x(W0,W0) = 1 − q_x^{−1}, vol(Iw_x) = vol(G(O_x))/(q_x+1), and ε(St⊗χ′,½,ψ_x) = −χ′(ϖ_x) for unramified χ′, which is the Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue. (c) For ramified quadratic η_x, ε(η_x,½,ψ_x) = q_x^{−1/2}Σ_{u∈k(x)^×}η_x(a′u)ψ_x(a′u) for any a′ with v(a′) = −1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): These are the explicit local inputs of Lemma 2.7 and Propositions 2.8–2.10: Casselman–Shalika for PGL2, the Steinberg Iwahori Whittaker vector and its Atkin–Lehner translate, and the Gauss-sum ε-factor. Items 23–25 cite them only inside proof steps.

items.name: Iwahori PGL_n shtukas with fractional infinity twist
items.statement: Assume (3.10)–(3.11). The groupoid Pic_X(k) acts on Sht^μ_n(Σ;D∞) by tensoring every E_i (with its flags) by L, using τL ≅ L. Set Sht^μ_G(Σ;D∞) := Sht^μ_n(Σ;D∞)/Pic_X(k) for G = PGL_n. It is the fibre product of (id, Fr): Bun_G(Σ) → Bun_G(Σ) × Bun_G(Σ) with (p_0, AL(−D∞)∘(p_r × id_{S∞})): Hk^μ_G(Σ) × S∞ → Bun_G(Σ) × Bun_G(Σ) (3.14). Π^μ_{n,D∞} descends to Π^μ_{G,D∞} = (π^μ_G, π_{G,∞}): Sht^μ_G(Σ;D∞) → X^r × S∞ (3.15).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Items 38, 41 and 43–78 concern the PGL_n stack, but item 34 defines only the GL_n stack Sht^μ_n(Σ;D∞), and no item defines the quotient, its Cartesian square or its leg map. Suggested owner: source route to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.2, which plans 'quotient central lattices when required' Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.

items.name: Atkin–Lehner automorphisms of Iwahori shtukas
items.statement: For x ∈ Σ, fractional twisting E† ↦ E†(−(1/n)x) (§3.1.1) is an automorphism of Bun_n(Σ) and of Hk^μ_n(Σ). It commutes with Frobenius pullback and with AL~(−D∞), so via (3.12) it induces an automorphism AL~_{Sht,x} of Sht^μ_n(Σ;D∞) over X^r × S∞, (E†_i, x_i, …) ↦ (E†_i(−(1/n)x), x_i, …). This descends to AL_{Sht,x} on Sht^μ_G(Σ;D∞). For n = 2 each AL_{Sht,x} is an involution of Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞), since twisting by −x is tensoring by O(−x); the AL_{Sht,x} (x ∈ Σ) commute; and they base-change to AL_{Sht′,x} on Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): §4.3 (pp. 459–460, Lemma 4.10 = item 88) and §4.4 (p. 461) use AL_{Sht,x}, but no item defines it. Suggested owner: source route to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.2 Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.

items.name: Atkin–Lehner involutions commute with Hecke operators
items.statement: For x ∈ Σ, the involutions AL_{Sht,x} of Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞) and AL_{Sht′,x} of Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞) induce involutions of Ch_{c,*}(Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞))_Q, Ch_{c,*}(Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞))_Q, H^*_c(Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞) ⊗ k̄, Q_ℓ) and H^*_c(Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞) ⊗ k̄, Q_ℓ). These involutions commute with the action of every f ∈ H^Σ_G.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): §4.4 (p. 461) uses it: 'Since AL_{Sht′,b} commutes with the action of any f ∈ H^Σ_G'. Suggested owner: source route to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.3 Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.

items.name: Hecke symmetry of the base-changed shtuka stack
items.statement: Let ν satisfy (3.16), and let Sht′ := Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞) = Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞) ×_{X^r×S∞} (X′^r × S′∞). It is smooth DM of dimension 2r (Proposition 3.10). For an effective divisor D on X − Σ let Sht′(h_D) be the base change of Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞;h_D), with projections p←′, p→′. (1) h_D ↦ (p←′ × p→′)_*[Sht′(h_D)] extends linearly to an action of H^Σ_G on Ch_{c,*}(Sht′)_Q (formalism of [YZ17, A.1.6], argument of [YZ17, Prop. 5.10]). (2) H^Σ_G ⊗ Q_ℓ acts on H^i_c(Sht′ ⊗ k̄, Q_ℓ) for every i, as in Proposition 3.15. (3) Each f ∈ H^Σ_G is self-adjoint for the intersection pairing on Ch_{c,*}(Sht′)_Q and for the cup-product pairing on H^{2r}_c(Sht′ ⊗ k̄, Q_ℓ)(r). (4) cl: Ch_{c,i}(Sht′)_Q → H^{4r−2i}_c(Sht′ ⊗ k̄, Q_ℓ)(2r − i) is H^Σ_G-equivariant for all i.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The main theorem works on Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞), but items 46, 47 and 49 cover only Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞), and item 48 mentions the base change only in passing. §5 (p. 476) uses the base-changed correspondences p←′ and p→′. Suggested owner: source route to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.3 Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.

items.name: Push-out and pull-back along the destabilizing line
items.statement: Let F be an unstable rank-two bundle on X_K (K algebraically closed), with maximal line subbundle L and M := F/L, and let D′ be an effective divisor. F⌟D′ is the push-out of 0 → L → F → M → 0 along L ↪ L(D′), and ⌜D′F is its pull-back along M(−D′) ↪ M. There is a canonical isomorphism F⌟D′ ≅ (⌜D′F)(D′), so both have the same image in Bun_G. If inst(F) > 0, then L(D′) and L are the maximal line subbundles of F⌟D′ and ⌜D′F, and inst(F⌟D′) = inst(⌜D′F) = inst(F) + deg D′ (as used in (3.26)).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Lemmas 3.19 and 3.21, Corollary 3.22 and Lemma 3.28 are all stated in terms of these operations, and no item defines them. Suggested owner: source route to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.0 Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.

items.name: Parabolic instability strata and truncations of Bun_G(Σ)
items.statement: For N > 0, NBun_G ⊂ Bun_G is the locally closed substack of E with inst(E) = N. Fix the canonical bijection Σ(k̄) ≅ Σ(K). For κ = (D,N) ∈ Z/2Z[Σ(k̄)] × Z_{>0}, κBun_G(Σ) ⊂ Bun_G(Σ) ⊗ k̄ is the locally closed substack of purely unstable E† with κ(E†) = κ. Order Z/2Z[Σ(k̄)] × Z by (D,N) ≤ (D′,N′) iff N′ − N ≥ |D − D′|, the number of points where D and D′ differ. ≤κBun_G(Σ) is the open substack of E† with inst(E(½D′)) ≤ N + |D′ − D| for all D′ ∈ Z/2Z[Σ(k̄)]. Then κBun_G(Σ) ⊂ ≤κ′Bun_G(Σ) iff κ ≤ κ′, and κBun_G(Σ) is closed in ≤κBun_G(Σ), with open complement <κBun_G(Σ).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Item 53 (Corollary 3.20) and items 180 and 56 use these strata, the order and the truncations, and no item defines them. Suggested owner: source route to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.0, which plans HN bounded opens but not this parabolic refinement Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.

items.name: Hecke action on the ind-perverse cohomology of shtukas
items.statement: Let D be an effective divisor on X − Σ of degree d, and let κ ≤ κ′ in K_r with κ′_i ≥ κ_i + d (degree part raised by d, divisor part equal) for all i. The fundamental cycle of Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞;h_D), as a cohomological correspondence between the constant sheaves on the truncations, induces K≤κ → K≤κ′. Taking pH^i and the colimit gives pH^i(h_D): pH^iK → pH^iK in Ind Perv((X^r × S∞) ⊗ k̄, Q_ℓ), and h_D ↦ pH^i(h_D) extends linearly to an action of H^Σ_G on pH^iK for every i (argument of [YZ17, Prop. 7.1] with Lemma 3.13(3)). The same correspondences act on each V≤i, compatibly with V≤i → V≤i+1 → V and with V≤i → H^{−i}(pH^iK).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 3.36 (item 69), Corollary 3.38 (item 71) and Proposition 3.39 (item 72) use the operators pH^i(h_D) and the H^Σ_G-equivariance of V≤i, and no item constructs them. Suggested owner: source route to GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.3 Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.

items.name: Section stacks over the root-Picard stack are affine bundles in high degree
items.statement: Let Q^{R′}_{X′} be the stack of pairs (L′, ϑ_{R′}) with L′ ∈ Pic_{X′} and ϑ_{R′} ∈ Γ(R′, L′|R′). Then Q^{R′}_{X′} ≅ Pic_{X′} ×_{Pic^{√R}_X} Pic^{√R;√R}_X via the root norm, and the norm map Q^{R′}_{X′} → Pic^{√R;√R}_X is smooth and relative DM. For n ≥ 2g′−1+ρ, the map X̂′_n → Q^{R′}_{X′}, (L′,s) ↦ (L′, s|R′), is an affine-space bundle of rank n−g′+1−ρ: for every geometric point, H^0(X′,L′) → H^0(R′,L′|R′) is surjective with kernel of dimension n−g′+1−ρ. Hence X̂′_n is smooth, and ν_β: X̂′_n → Pic^{√R;√R}_X is smooth and relative DM. Likewise, for n ≥ 2g−1+ρ, ÂJ^{√R;√R}_n: X̂^{√R}_n → Pic^{√R;√R,n}_X is an affine-space bundle of rank n−ρ−g+1.
items.locator: §5.1.4, proof of Proposition 5.5(1), p. 467; also proof of Proposition 6.2(2), p. 495
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): This is the Riemann–Roch input behind the smoothness of M_d (items 94, 114) and of N_d (item 126). No item states it. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Divisor map δ and the fibre A♭_D
items.statement: δ: A♭_d → U_d sends (Δ,a,b) to the divisor of a−b viewed as a nonzero section of Δ(−R), which has degree d. Conditions (1)–(3) of Definitions 5.3/5.4 imply that this divisor avoids Σ ∪ R. For an effective divisor D on U = X−Σ−R of degree d, set A♭_D := δ^{-1}(D) ⊂ A♭_d.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): A♭_D is the index set of the trace formula (items 121, 130–133), and δ is used throughout §6. No item defines them. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Generic incidence description of H±
