items.statement: Let A♦_d := (X^{√R}_{d+ρ−N−} ×_{Pic^{√R;√R}_X} X^{√R}_{d+ρ−N+}) ∩ A_d, the open locus where a ≠ 0 and b ≠ 0; let M♦_d := f_d^{-1}(A♦_d) and H♦± := H±|_{A♦_d}. For n ≥ 0, let I′_n = {(D,x′) ∈ X′_n × X′ : x′ ∈ D}, with ←i(D,x′) = D and →i(D,x′) = D+σ(x′)−x′ (5.12). Then over M♦_d, H♦+ is the restriction to A♦_d of X′_{d+ρ−N−} ×_{Pic^{√R;√R}_X} I′_{d+ρ−N+}, and H♦− is that of I′_{d+ρ−N−} ×_{Pic^{√R;√R}_X} X′_{d+ρ−N+}. In particular dim H♦± = dim M♦_d = 2d+ρ−N−g+1, and f_d is finite over A♦_d.
items.locator: §5.1.5, (5.12), pp. 469–470; A♦_d defined in the proof of Proposition 5.5(4), p. 468, and p. 469
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Items 99/100 use the ♦-loci only as a closure convention. The identification of H♦± with the pullback of the incidence correspondence I′ (cf. YZ17 Lemma 6.3), and dim H♦± = m, are what Proposition 7.2 (items 144/145) and the proof of Theorem 5.6 use. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Determinant divisor s and Atkin–Lehner on H_d(Σ)
items.statement: s: H_d(Σ) → U_d records the divisor of det(ϕ) as a section of det(E)^{-1}⊗det(E′). It lies in U because ϕ is an isomorphism along (Σ ⊔ R)×S, and it is invariant under the Pic_X action. AL_{H,∞}: H_d(Σ)×S∞ → H_d(Σ) applies AL_{G,∞} of (3.20) to both E† and E′† and keeps ϕ.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The map s is what makes (5.22) possible, and AL_{H,∞} enters α_H in (5.18). Neither is defined in items 185–189. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Level divisors D±({x′(1)})
items.statement: For {x′(1)}_{x′∈Σ′∞} ∈ S′∞(S), with x′(j) = x′(j−1)∘Fr_S and d_x = deg x, set D+({x′(1)}) := Σ_{x∈Σf∩Σ+} µ′_x×S + Σ_{x∈Σ∞∩Σ+} E_x. Here µ′_x ∈ Σ′_f is the point over x chosen by µ′_f. E_x = Γ_{x′(1)}+…+Γ_{x′(d_x)} if µ′_x = 1, and E_x = Γ_{x′(d_x+1)}+…+Γ_{x′(2d_x)} if µ′_x = −1. This is a relative divisor of degree N+ on X′×S. D−({x′(1)}) is given by the same formula with Σ− in place of Σ+; it has degree N−. Both lie over Σ±×S.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): D± are the level divisors in Lemma 5.13 (item 103), in Ξ_M (item 105) and in Proposition 5.16. Item 103 mentions them only by name. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Sht′^r_{H,d}(Σ;Σ∞)
items.statement: Sht′^r_{H,d}(Σ;Σ∞) := H_d(Σ) ×_{(id,Fr), H_d(Σ)×H_d(Σ), (p′_{H,0},α_H)} (Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ)×S′∞), the Cartesian square (5.20), where α_H = AL_{H,∞}∘(p′_{H,r}×ν∞). Via ←→q′ it maps to Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞)×_{S′∞}Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞), and θ′^µ×θ′^{µ′} maps Sht^µ_T(µ∞·Σ′∞)×_{S′∞}Sht^{µ′}_T(µ′∞·Σ′∞) to the same target (5.21).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): It is the third-column fibre product of (5.18), used in (5.21), (5.22), (5.27) and (5.46). Items 186–189 define the other fibre products but not this one. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Decomposition of Sht′^r_{H,d} by the determinant divisor
items.statement: The Hecke correspondence Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ) preserves s: H_d(Σ) → U_d, and Frobenius on H_d(Σ) covers Frobenius on U_d. Hence Sht′^r_{H,d}(Σ;Σ∞) decomposes over U_d(k) (effective divisors of degree d on U), and the piece indexed by D is canonically Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞;h_D): Sht′^r_{H,d}(Σ;Σ∞) = ⊔_{D∈U_d(k)} Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞;h_D).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): This identifies the D-piece of the Frobenius fixed locus with the Hecke correspondence Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞;h_D), so it is the bridge from Theorem 5.20 to I^{µ,µ′}(h_D). It is stated with 'as in [YZ17, Lemma 6.12] one shows' and no item covers it. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Column presentation and D-decomposition of Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,d}
items.statement: Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,d}, defined as the fibre product (5.26), is also the fibre product of (5.21): the square (5.27) with Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,d} → Sht′^r_{H,d}(Σ;Σ∞) and θ′^µ×θ′^{µ′} is Cartesian. Consequently Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,d} = ⊔_{D∈U_d(k)} Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,D} (5.28), where Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,D} = (Sht^µ_T(µ∞·Σ′∞)×_{S′∞}Sht^{µ′}_T(µ′∞·Σ′∞)) ×_{Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞)×_{S′∞}Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞)} Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞;h_D) along θ′^µ×θ′^{µ′} and (←p′,→p′) (5.29).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Needed to pass from ζ on Hk^{µ,µ′}_{M,d} to the cycles θ′^µ, θ′^{µ′} on Sht′ (the proofs of Theorem 5.20 and of Proposition 5.17(8)). Item 189 defines Sht_{M,d} only as the row fibre product. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: The cycle ζ
items.statement: Using Proposition 5.17(2),(4),(6): dim Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ) + dim(Hk^µ_T×Hk^{µ′}_T×S′∞) − 2 dim Hk′^r_G(Σ) = m = 2d+ρ−N−g+1. Define ζ := (θ^{µ,µ′}_{Hk})^![Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ)] ∈ Ch_m(Hk^{µ,µ′}_{M,d})_Q, the refined Gysin pullback along the Cartesian square (5.24). It is defined because (5.24) satisfies YZ17 §A.2.8 (Proposition 5.18).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): ζ is the cycle of Lemma 5.19 and Theorem 5.20 (items 118, 119); it needs its own definition node with the dimension identity. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Local intersection number with the Frobenius graph
items.statement: Since M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ) is smooth DM (Proposition 5.17(7)), (id,Fr): M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ) → M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)^2 is a regular local immersion, and (id,Fr)^!ζ ∈ Ch_0(Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,d}) is defined. Its D-component lies in Ch_0(Sht^{µ,µ′}_{M,D}), which is proper over k (Proposition 5.17(8)). Set ⟨ζ,Γ(Fr_{M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)})⟩_D := deg((id,Fr)^!ζ)_D ∈ Q.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): This is the left side of Theorem 5.20; no item defines it. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Intersection number as a Gysin degree on Sht′(h_D)
items.statement: For D an effective divisor on U: (Π_{x′∈Σ′∞} d_{x′})·I^{µ,µ′}(h_D) = deg((θ′^µ×θ′^{µ′})^![Sht′^r_G(Σ;Σ∞;h_D)]), the refined Gysin pullback along the Cartesian square (5.29).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): This expresses the intersection number of Heegner–Drinfeld cycles as a refined Gysin degree on the Hecke correspondence. The paper says it is 'easy to see', and no item states it (item 90 is Lemma 4.14, a different formula). Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: The Frobenius-graph pullback of the H-Hecke stack is the fundamental class
items.statement: (id,Fr_{H_d(Σ)})^![Hk′^r_{H,d}(Σ)×S′∞] = [Sht′^r_{H,d}(Σ;Σ∞)] in Ch_*(Sht′^r_{H,d}(Σ;Σ∞))_Q. Proof: over (U_d×X^r)°, Sht′^r_{H,d} is ⊔_D Sht^r_G(Σ;Σ∞;h_D)|_{(X−D)^r} ×_{X^r} X′^r, which is smooth of the expected dimension 2r (Lemma 3.13(2)). By Lemma 3.13(3) the fibres over X^r×S∞ have dimension r, so the complement has dimension < 2r.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): A separate cycle identity (analogue of YZ17 Lemma 6.14(2)) with its own dimension argument. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Transfer of ⟨ζ,Γ(Fr)⟩_D to M_d
items.statement: Assume d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}. Let H̄♦_{µµ′} be the closure of H_{µµ′}|_{A♦_d}. Then ⟨ζ,Γ(Fr_{M_d(µΣ,µ′Σ)})⟩_D = deg(S′∞)·⟨[H̄♦_{µµ′}],Γ(Fr_{M_d})⟩_D, with deg S′∞ = Π_{x′∈Σ′∞} d_{x′}. Proof: (5.47) moves AL_{M,∞} into the horizontal arrow; via Ξ_M and Ξ_H it becomes (5.50) (Proposition 5.15(2)); ζ♯ equals the fundamental class over A♦_d (Lemma 5.19); and by Proposition 5.5(4) the complement of M♦_d×_{A♦_d}M♦_d in M_d×_{A_d}M_d has dimension < dim M_d.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): This reduces Theorem 5.20 to the untwisted trace on M_d: the Atkin–Lehner transfer, Lemma 5.19 and the smallness replacement of ζ♯ by the closure cycle. No item covers it. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Cohomological composition of incidence correspondences
items.statement: For d ≥ 3g−2+N: f_{d,!}[H̄♦_{µµ′}] = (f_{d,!}[H̄♦+])^{r+}∘(f_{d,!}[H̄♦−])^{r−} in End(Rf_{d,!}Q_ℓ), hence also after RΩ_! on Rf♭_{d,!}Q_ℓ. Over A♦_d, [H̄♦_{µµ′}] is the composition of r+ copies of [H̄♦+] and r− copies of [H̄♦−] in any order. The complement of M♦_d×_{A♦_d}M♦_d in M_d×_{A_d}M_d has dimension < dim M_d (Proposition 5.5(4)), so the two cohomological correspondences agree.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): This is the step that turns the single correspondence H_{µµ′} into the product of powers of H+ and H− in (5.14). It relies on H+ and H− acting on different factors over A♦_d, so that they commute, and on smallness. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Orbital sum at an invariant u
items.statement: For u ∈ P^1(F)−{1} and h ∈ C_c^∞(G(A)), J(u,h,s1,s2) := Σ_{γ∈A(F)\G(F)/A(F), inv(γ)=u} J(γ,h,s1,s2). For u ∉ {0,1,∞} there is exactly one such γ, represented by γ̃(u) = [[1,u],[1,1]]. For u = 0 there are three, 1, n+ = [[1,1],[0,1]], n− = [[1,0],[1,1]]; for u = ∞ there are three, w0, n+w0, n−w0.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 6.3 (items 131–133) is stated for J(u,…), which no item defines. Item 14 defines only the distribution J(f,s1,s2). Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Global square-root presentation of h̃^{Σ±}_D
items.statement: Set Ξ_{D,x} = Ξ_x (§2.4.1) for x ∈ R, Ξ_{D,x} = J̃_x for x ∈ Σ, and Ξ_{D,x} = Mat_2(O_x)_{v_x(det)=n_x} otherwise, where n_x is the multiplicity of x in D. Let Ξ_D = Π_x Ξ_{D,x}, with projection µ: Ξ_D → Mat_2(O)_{div(det)=D+R}. Then h̃^{Σ±}_D = h̃_D·(⊗_{x∈R} h̃^□_x)⊗(⊗_{x∈Σ} 1_{J̃_x}) equals µ_*1_{Ξ_D}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The global form of Lemma 2.4 (item 19). It is the identity that converts the orbital integral into a count over X̃_{D,γ̃}, and it is where det ψ_R = 0 (E23) enters. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Integral over a groupoid with finite automorphisms
items.statement: For a groupoid G with finite automorphism groups and a finitely supported function f on its isomorphism classes, ∫_G f := Σ_{g∈π0(G)} f(g)/#Aut(g).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 6.4 and the trace-formula steps (items 136–138) are identities of groupoid-weighted sums. The integral needs a definition node. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Pushforward compatibility of groupoid integrals
items.statement: If ϕ: G → G′ is a functor of groupoids with finite automorphism groups and f is a finitely supported function on G, then ∫_G f = ∫_{G′} ϕ_!f, where (ϕ_!f)(g′) := ∫_{ϕ^{-1}(g′)} f|_{ϕ^{-1}(g′)} and ϕ^{-1}(g′) is the homotopy fibre groupoid.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Pushforward compatibility of the groupoid integral, used for λ: X_{D,γ} → Div^{√R}(X)^3. Note the misprint E24 (f lives on G, not G′). Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Haar integral as a groupoid integral
items.statement: Let H be a locally compact group with Haar measure dh, and ϕ: H1 → H a homomorphism from a compact group with open image and finite kernel. The action groupoid H/H1 is discrete with automorphism groups ≅ ker ϕ, and for f on H right-invariant under ϕ(H1): ∫_H f(h)dh = vol(ϕ(H1),dh)·#ker(ϕ)·∫_{H/H1} f̄ (6.14). For H = (A^×)^3, H1 = (O^×_{√R})^3 and vol(O^×) = 1, the constant is 1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Converts the adelic integral (6.12) into the groupoid sum; the normalisation constant is 1 because kernel and cokernel of O^×_{√R} → O^× both have order 2^{#R}. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Orbital groupoid equals the Hitchin-type fibre
items.statement: Let u ∈ P^1(F)−{0,1,∞} and γ̃(u) = [[1,u],[1,1]]. The functor λ: X_{D,γ̃(u)} → ⊔_{d∈Q_d} N_d(k) sends (E♮1,E♮2,E′♮1,E′♮2,ψ_R) to (AJ^{√R}(−E♮1), …, AJ^{√R}(−E′♮2), ϕ, ψ_R), with X_{D,γ̃} corrected by det ψ_R = 0 (item 135). It lands in g♭_d^{-1}(a) with inv_D(a) = u. Hence X_{D,γ̃(u)} = ∅ if u ∉ inv_D(A♭_D(k)). If u = inv_D(a), λ is an equivalence onto N_{d,a}(k) := ⊔_{d∈Q_d} (g♭_d)^{-1}(a)(k). The inverse normalises L′♮2 = O_X˙ and reads off E1, E2, E′1 from the nonzero sections ϕ21, ϕ22, ϕ11.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Item 137 assumes this isomorphism ('Under X_(D,γ̃) ≅ coproduct N_d,a(k)') without stating it. It is the geometric heart of Theorem 6.3(1)–(2). Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Relaxed stacks N̂_d and the unipotent fibres
items.statement: Assume Σ− = ∅ and let a0 = (O_X(D+R),1,0) ∈ A♭_D(k), the unique point with inv_D = 0. Q̂_d ⊂ Z^4 is defined like Q_d but without d_ij ≥ 0. For d ∈ Q̂_d, N̂_d is defined like N_d but without condition (5) of Definition 6.1, requiring instead that at most one ϕ_ij is zero; ĝ♭_d: N̂_d → A_d → A♭_d. N̂_{d,a0} := (ĝ♭_d)^{-1}(a0) = N̂+_{d,a0} ⊔ N̂−_{d,a0}, where N̂+ has ϕ21 = 0, ϕ12 ≠ 0 and N̂− has ϕ12 = 0, ϕ21 ≠ 0. As in §6.2.4 there are equivalences λ±: X_{D,n±} ≅ ⊔_{d∈Q̂_d} N̂±_{d,a0}(k), and N±_{d,a0} := N̂±_{d,a0} ∩ N_{d,a0}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): These objects carry the singular orbits in Theorem 6.3(3) (item 133) and Lemma 6.5 (item 138); no item defines them. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Product decomposition of the unipotent fibre
items.statement: Let (X^{√R}_{d11}×X^{√R}_{d22−N−})_{D+R} be the fibre over D+R of X^{√R}_{d11}×X^{√R}_{d22−N−} → X^{√R}_{d+ρ−N−} → X_{d+ρ−N−} (addition, then coarse map). Recording (L♮ij,ϕij,ψ_{ij,R}) for (i,j) = (1,1),(2,2),(1,2) gives an isomorphism N̂+_{d,a0} ≅ (X^{√R}_{d11}×X^{√R}_{d22−N−})_{D+R} × X^{√R}_{d12}; then L♮21 is determined and ϕ21 = 0. Similarly N̂−_{d,a0} ≅ (X^{√R}_{d11}×X^{√R}_{d22−N−})_{D+R} × X^{√R}_{d21−N+}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The factorisation behind Lemma 6.5(1)–(2) and (6.23). Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Vanishing of the identity orbital integral
items.statement: J(1, h^{Σ±}_D, s1, s2) = 0, because the character (t,t′) ↦ |tt′|^{s1}|t′/t|^{s2}η(t) of A(A)×A(A) is nontrivial on the stabilizer of 1 (the diagonal A(A)). Consequently J(0,h^{Σ±}_D,s1,s2) = J(n+,…)+J(n−,…) (6.24), and similarly at u = ∞.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Split from item 138: a separate statement with a separate proof (nontrivial character on the stabilizer). Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz for proper maps of DM stacks with local systems
items.statement: Let g: N → A be a proper morphism from a DM stack of finite type over k = F_q to a scheme, L a constructible Q_ℓ-sheaf on N, and a ∈ A(k). Then Σ_{Λ∈g^{-1}(a)(k)} Tr(Fr_Λ, L_Λ)/#Aut(Λ) = Tr(Fr_a, (Rg_!L)_a). Applied to g♭_d and L_d, whose trace function is η(L♮11)η(L♮12) by Proposition A.12, this gives Σ_{Λ∈N_{d,a}(k)} η(L♮11)η(L♮12)/#Aut(Λ) = Tr(Fr_a, (Rg♭_{d,!}L_d)_a).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 6.3 is obtained by applying a groupoid-weighted Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula for a proper map from a finite-type DM stack to a scheme, with a rank-one local system. Item 120 (YZ17 Proposition A.12) is the correspondence version with Q_ℓ coefficients and does not cover it. The scheme case belongs to the Tau Ceti TraceFormula roadmap (PR 196) that EDC.8 cites; the DM-stack weighting is not planned. Suggested owner:  Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Smallness and decomposition of the root norm pushforward
items.statement: Let n ≥ max{2g′−1, 2g′−g}. The map ν̂^√R_n: X̂′_n → X̂^√R_n of (A.10) is proper and small. Its only positive-dimensional fibres lie over the zero section Pic^{√R,n}_X ⊂ X̂^√R_n, which has codimension n−g+1. There they are fibres of Nm^√R_{X′/X}: Pic^n_{X′} → Pic^{√R,n}_X, of dimension g′−g, and n−g+1 ≥ 2(g′−g)+1. Since X̂′_n is smooth and geometrically connected of dimension n, Rν̂^√R_{n,!}Q̄_ℓ[n] is the middle extension of its restriction to X^{√R,◦}_n. There is a canonical isomorphism Rν̂^√R_{n,!}Q̄_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n} K_{n,i}, induced over X^{√R,◦}_n by (7.1).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The key sheaf-theoretic input to Proposition 7.1(2) (the ramified analogue of YZ17 Prop. 8.2, (8.5)). No item states it. The paper asserts it for d′ ≥ 2g′−g, but its proof needs d′ ≥ 2g′−1 as well (see new issue). Suggested owner: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (this paper's part-ii route) Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Irreducibility of the comparison base A_d
items.statement: Let d ≥ 2g−1+N and n = d+ρ−N±. The fibre of ÂJ^{√R;√R}_n: X̂^√R_n → Pic^{√R;√R,n}_X over (L, K_R, ι, α_R) is the affine space {a ∈ H^0(X,L) : a|_R = ι(α_R^{⊗2})}. It is a torsor under H^0(X, L(−R)), of dimension n−ρ−g+1. Hence the maps ν_a, ν_b of (5.4) are affine-space bundles over the irreducible stack Pic^{√R;√R,d+ρ}_X. So X̂^√R_{d+ρ−N−} ×_{Pic^{√R;√R,d+ρ}_X} X̂^√R_{d+ρ−N+} is irreducible, and so is its open substack A_d.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Used to pass from 'middle extension from some open' to 'from any non-empty open' in Propositions 7.1(1), 7.2 and 7.3(1). Asserted in one line and covered by no item. Suggested owner: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (this paper's part-ii route) Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Eigenvalues of the norm incidence operator
items.statement: For n ≥ 0 let I′_n = {(D, x′) ∈ X′_n × X′ : x′ ∈ D}, with ←i(D,x′) = D and →i(D,x′) = D + σ(x′) − x′ (5.12). Let T_n = ν^√R_{n,!}[I′_n] be the induced endomorphism of Rν^√R_{n,!}Q̄_ℓ on X^√R_n. Under Rν^√R_{n,!}Q̄_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{i=0}^{n} K_{n,i}|_{X^√R_n}, T_n preserves each summand and acts on K_{n,i} by the scalar n − 2i. At a geometric generic point the stalk is Q̄_ℓ[Γ_n/S_n], spanned by monomials x_1^{ε_1}⋯x_n^{ε_n}. There T_n is a derivation fixing x_i^+ + x_i^− and negating x_i^+ − x_i^−, so it acts on P_δ = ∏_i (x_i^+ + δ_i x_i^−) by n − 2|δ|.
items.locator: §7.1, proof of Proposition 7.2, p. 507 (from [YZ17, Prop. 8.3, pp. 870–872])
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 7.2 is reduced to this computation ('the rest of the argument is the same as [10, Prop. 8.3]'). Items 144–145 state only the conclusion. Suggested owner: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (this paper's part-ii route) Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Addition pushforward of the quadratic symmetric local systems
items.statement: Let L be the quadratic local system of ν on X^√R_1 (§A.3.4) and L_i its symmetric powers (§A.2.1). For i, j ≥ 0 there is a canonical isomorphism add^√R_{i,j,!}(L_i ⊠ Q̄_ℓ) ≅ K_{i+j,i}|_{X^√R_{i+j}} on X^√R_{i+j}. Both sides are shifted middle extensions, since add^√R_{i,j} is finite and surjective with smooth irreducible source. The isomorphism is the one over (X−R)^◦_{i+j} from [YZ17, Prop. 8.5]: there add^◦ is the quotient of the Γ_{i+j}-cover by S_i × S_j, and L_i ⊠ Q̄_ℓ corresponds to ρ_{i+j,i}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The identity that turns the orbital side into IC sheaves (the ramified analogue of YZ17 Prop. 8.5, (8.9)). No item states it. Suggested owner: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (this paper's part-ii route) Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Zero-leg Iwahori shtukas and automorphic forms of level K
items.statement: Let K = ∏_{x∉Σ} G(O_x) × ∏_{x∈Σ} Iw_x and let A(K) be the Q-vector space of compactly supported functions on G(F)\G(A)/K. The zero-leg stack Sht^0_G(Σ) (with Σ_∞ = ∅) is the discrete groupoid G(F)\G(A)/K, so A(K)⊗Q_ℓ ≅ H^0_c(Sht^0_G(Σ)⊗k̄, Q_ℓ), H^Σ_G-equivariantly. The image of H^Σ_G in End(A(K)) is a finitely generated Q-algebra of Krull dimension one (Corollary 3.40 with r = 0). Further, A(K)⊗Q̄_ℓ = A(K)_Eis⊗Q̄_ℓ ⊕ ⊕_{π∈Π_Σ(Q̄_ℓ)} A(K)_π (Theorem 3.41). Here Π_Σ(Q̄_ℓ) is the set of cuspidal automorphic representations of G(A) with Q̄_ℓ-coefficients and nonzero K-fixed vectors, and A(K)_π = π^K.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The automorphic factor of H̃^Σ_ℓ and the source of e_π's automorphic meaning. It is not stated by any item (item 151 alludes to it). Suggested owner: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (this paper's part-ii route) Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Strong multiplicity one for PGL_2 over function fields
items.statement: Let π, π′ be cuspidal automorphic representations of PGL_2(A_F), F = k(X), with π_x ≅ π′_x for all x outside a finite set of places. Then π = π′. Consequently λ_π: H^Σ_G → Q̄_ℓ, and even its restriction to H^{Σ∪R}_G, determines π ∈ Π_Σ(Q̄_ℓ), and Π_Σ(Q̄_ℓ) ⊂ Spec(H^Σ_G ⊗ Q̄_ℓ).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Cited without statement and used twice. An extension of E28 needs it with the extra excluded places R. No item covers it. Suggested owner: an automorphic function-field layer (FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.6 area) or ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (this paper's part-ii route) Route: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil.

items.name: Coarse moduli of root symmetric powers
items.statement: The restriction ω^√R_d: X^√R_d → X_d of ω̂^√R_d realizes X_d as the coarse moduli scheme of X^√R_d. In particular X^√R_1 is a smooth DM curve with coarse moduli space X; it is isomorphic to X over X−R, and its points over R have automorphism group μ_2.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Used in §A.2 to translate local systems on X^√R_1 into local systems on X−R, and throughout for point counts. Not stated by any item. Suggested owner: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory (this paper's part-ii route) Route: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory.

items.name: Smoothness criterion for maps to products of [A^1/G_m]
items.statement: Let Z be a smooth irreducible k-scheme and let f_i: Z → [A^1/G_m] (1 ≤ i ≤ n) be morphisms whose images do not lie in [{0}/G_m], so that the D_i = f_i^{−1}([{0}/G_m]) are effective Cartier divisors. Then f = (f_1, …, f_n): Z → [A^n/G_m^n] is smooth if and only if the D_i are smooth and intersect transversely, i.e. every nonempty D_I = ∩_{i∈I} D_i is smooth of codimension #I.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The general criterion behind Lemma A.4. Not stated by any item. Suggested owner: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory (this paper's part-ii route) Route: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory.

items.name: Root Abel–Jacobi maps
items.statement: Forgetting a gives ÂJ^{√R;√R}_d: X̂^√R_d → Pic^{√R;√R,d}_X, (L♮, a, α_R) ↦ (L♮, α_R). Forgetting α_R as well gives ÂJ^√R_d: X̂^√R_d → Pic^{√R,d}_X. AJ^{√R;√R}_d and AJ^√R_d are their restrictions to X^√R_d. For R = ∅, AJ^√R_d is the usual Abel–Jacobi map X_d → Pic^d_X.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Used in Lemmas A.9–A.10, Proposition A.11, (5.4), §6.2.1 and item 184. No item defines them. Suggested owner: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory (this paper's part-ii route) Route: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory.

items.name: Rank-one local systems on the root curve
items.statement: Restriction to X−R is an equivalence between rank-one Q̄_ℓ-local systems on X^√R_1 and rank-one Q̄_ℓ-local systems on X−R on which the inertia at each x ∈ R acts through a character of order dividing 2. Such characters are necessarily tame, since p ≠ 2.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): Needed to define L on X^√R_1 from L_{X′/X}|_{X−R} (§A.3.4). Not stated by any item. Suggested owner: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory (this paper's part-ii route) Route: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory.

items.name: Simple connectivity of weighted punctured-affine quotients
items.statement: Let K be algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ 2, ρ ≥ 1 and n ≥ ρ+1. Let G_m act on M = A^n − {0} with weight 2 on the first n−ρ coordinates and weight 1 on the last ρ. Then every connected finite étale cover of [M/G_m] is an isomorphism. The proof pulls back along P^{n−1} → [M/G_m], [x, y] ↦ [x², y], a branched μ_2^{n−ρ}-cover. Applied to M = H^0(X,L)◦ ×_{H^0(R,L_R)} H^0(R,K_R), the fibre of AJ^√R_d when d ≥ ρ + max{2g−1, 1}, it shows that L_d is trivial on the fibres of AJ^√R_d.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The geometric heart of the descent in Lemma A.9. Not stated by any item. Suggested owner: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory (this paper's part-ii route) Route: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory.

items.name: Root multiplicative sheaf
items.statement: With i_R: R ↪ X, set G^√R_{m,X} := G_{m,X} ×_{i_{R*}G_{m,R}, [2]} i_{R*}G_{m,R}, a fibre product of étale sheaves on X along restriction and squaring. Pic^√R_X is the moduli stack of G^√R_{m,X}-torsors.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The torsor description of Pic^√R_X used for the norm and for (A.11). Item 174 uses it without a definition. Suggested owner: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory (this paper's part-ii route) Route: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory.

items.name: The quadratic local system and character of ν
items.statement: ν_*Q̄_ℓ = Q̄_ℓ ⊕ L_{X′/X}, the σ-eigensheaves for the eigenvalues 1 and −1. L_{X′/X}|_{X−R} is a rank-one local system with monodromy in {±1}, ramified exactly along R. L denotes the corresponding local system on X^√R_1; it is geometrically nontrivial because X′ is geometrically connected. The idele class character η_{F′/F} of F′ = k(X′) is trivial on the image of O^×_{√R}: at x ∈ R its restriction to O^×_x is the Legendre symbol of the residue. It therefore factors through F^×\A^×_F/O^×_{√R}, which is π_0 of Pic^√R_X(k) (Lemma A.5).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 (coverage of the paper): The objects compared in Proposition A.12. Item 175 states only the comparison. Suggested owner: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory (this paper's part-ii route) Route: RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory.

routes.reason: GS.0 owns bundles, Iwahori flags and HN strata; GS.1 owns global minuscule Hecke geometry; GS.2 owns Frobenius/fractional-infinity shtukas and local models; GS.3 owns their compact cohomology, truncation colimits and spectral finiteness. This paper adds precise PGL2 horocycle and Eisenstein-sector proofs within those targets. Generic modulo-constructible categorical definitions come from the separate EDC extension, not a duplicate shtuka-specific Ind category. All corrected finite-type/high-instability cases remain required.

Follow the already proposed YZ17 GZ.5 toric-period/relative-trace source route: add the ramified h-sharp/f-sharp tests, Iwahori local factors, two-variable toric regularization and exact adjoint/measure normalization. Import generic automorphic spaces and fixed-level finiteness from FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.6, generic standard L-factors from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2, and adeles/Haar conventions from FA.2. Do not create a second automorphic or L-function foundation. The degree-spanning lemma is the algebraic analytic-comparison input; cycle intersections stay in the shared shtuka extension.

The paper consumes the scheme/line-bundle, cohomology/base-change and Picard comparison contracts, not merely the existing function-field Riemann–Roch statement. SF.3 integrates the upstream AlgebraicCurves/JacobianChallenge owners. No upstream roadmap is replanned; the tame Hurwitz input is separately marked planned in its upstream layer.

Import the constructible perverse category, normalized IC, pure geometric decomposition and small-map consequences. The paper-specific support inequalities, canonical constant-term identification and ramified comparison computations remain with their consuming route. The additional ind/Serre-quotient formalism is not hidden inside the bounded constructible stage.

SF.1 owns quotient/root-stack geometry and infinitesimal fibres; use its existing Bresciani24 root-stack source lead rather than rebuilding roots inside geometric class field theory. SF.5 owns rational DM-stack Chow/refined-Gysin, support-filtered coherent K0 and the YZ17 octahedron contract. The ramified master diagram only supplies its particular instantiation. A_ d's root fibre and finite flat presentations must retain their stack hypotheses.

The generic smooth-DM correspondence/Frobenius-graph identity is precisely the trace/cycle-class interface already sourced from YZ17. Retain its proper, representable-left-projection, smooth/separated-M and SCHEME-base hypotheses. The numerical application over A_d^flat is not another trace-formula foundation.

routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: special cycles on shtuka moduli and the higher Siegel–Weil formula
routes.reason: Reuse exactly the Part II candidate already proposed by PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17 and PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24; this is an additional ramified/Iwahori toric branch of that proposal, not a second design. No atlas stage yet supplies these cycle/intersection identities. Generic GS, EDC, SF and ramified class-field foundations remain imported.
routes.brief:
Extend the EXISTING ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil proposal, retaining both its even-leg unramified Yun–Zhang17 branch and its unitary Feng–Yun–Zhang24 higher Siegel–Weil branch. Add the ramified PGL2 branch of Yun–Zhang19, not a new parallel roadmap. Standing data: k=Fq, p≠2, X and X′ smooth projective geometrically connected, ν:X′→X of degree two with reduced ramification R of degreeρ; Σ disjoint from R, N=degΣ, Σ∞ the inert closed places and Σf the split ones. π is PGL2 cuspidal, unramified outside Σ and an unramified quadratic twist of Steinberg at Σ. Require r≥0 and r≡#Σ∞ mod2; # counts closed places, not their degrees. For μ,μ′∈T_(r,Σ), r± count agreeing/disagreeing leg signs and ε− is the product of π⊗η Atkin–Lehner signs at differing level places. Define ℒtwo=ℒπ(s1+s2+1/2)ℒπη(s1−s2+1/2), where normalization exponents are 2g−2+N/2 and 2g−2+N/2+ρ. The endpoint Theorem1.2 is C ε− ∂s1^r+∂s2^r−ℒtwo(0,0)=⟨Zπ^μ(ξ),Zπ^μ′(ξ)⟩, with C=q^−(2g−2)q^(ρ/2−N)/(2(−logq)^rL(π,Ad,1)). Theorem1.3 is C ℒπ^(r1)(1/2)ℒπη^(r−r1)(1/2)=⟨ε_r1Zπ^μ,ε_r1Zπ^μ⟩, with ε_r1=∏i≤r1(1+σi)/2∏j>r1(1−σj)/2. Corollary1.4 has the pushdown factor 2^(r−1), as item155 states. These are ordinary algebraic intersections over finite fields, not arithmetic-height/Arakelov formulas. Cover the torus quotient GROUPoid and Lang torsors, root-sensitive flags and AL maps, proper cycles and ξ-normalization, M_d/A_d/A_d^flat, signed incidence correspondences, ramified Hom description valid on nonreduced bases, the full octahedron master diagram, N_dquad with detψ_R=0 and degree cutoffs, weighted orbital groupoids and regular/singular trace identities, ordered Γ_d covers and normalized K_(d,i), smallness only for f_d, boundary IC estimates for g_d, eigenvalues B−2j/A−2i, the allowed-Hecke comparison and spectral projector, and the Walsh proof with C retained. Import Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.0–3) for all moduli/Hecke/HN/spectral foundations; Scheme and stack foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1/3/5) for roots, Picard geometry and refined Gysin/octahedron; Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5/7/8) plus its IndConstructibles extension; Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.2/4/5/6) and its RamifiedGeometricClassFieldTheory extension; Gross–Zagier and arithmetic heights (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5) for the normalized ramified toric comparison. Tests must include r=0, r=1 with an odd number of inert places, a degree-two inert place for the parity trap, all-ones residue root counts 8 versus16, d=2 ordered/symmetric cover degrees8 versus4, μ≠μ′ cross-pairings, r1=0/r projector endpoints, and the negative exponent/incidence sign. Gates G1–G7 are mandatory remaining proof work. Do not present (1.9), Conjecture1.6 or announced BSD applications as proved. Do not claim that r=1 is a specialization of the even-r first paper.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19), to respect when stating the layers: Remark 4.5 is false when Σ∞ = ∅ (define the stack by square (4.3) or the §4.1.5 base change); the application of Theorem 2.2 / Lemma 2.3 in (7.10) needs a repair through Lemma 2.6, since h□ at R is not left Iwahori-invariant; 'Sht = ⋃ ≤κSht' fails when r < #Σ∞ (E10); (5.5) is not an open embedding when R ≠ ∅; Lemma 6.4 is false as printed (E23); and the extraction's repair of Theorem 7.5 (E28) must also exclude extra eigenspaces that agree with π away from R, which strong multiplicity one alone does not do.

routes.title: Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations, Part II: ramified geometric class field theory
routes.reason: FA.4 supplies arithmetic reciprocity and norm subgroups, not the root-Picard character SHEAF and all-degree Abel–Jacobi descent of AppendixA. SF.1 supplies generic root stacks but not this multiplicative local-system construction. A single reusable geometric class-field extension supplies the PGL2 comparison and future rank-one ramified consumers.
routes.brief: Start after Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic), especially FA.2/4: import its adelic/idele and arithmetic reciprocity objects, without rebuilding them. Construct the geometric refinement in Yun–Zhang19 AppendixA for square-root ramification on a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a finite field of odd characteristic. The final contracts are LemmaA.11's multiplicative rank-one local system L_Pic on the graded root-Picard stack, with unit, associativity and commutativity, and PropositionA.12's equality of its Frobenius trace with η_(F′/F) for a geometrically connected quadratic cover. The character-sheaf construction starts with ANY rank-one Qℓbar local system on the root curve, equivalently ramification monodromy of order dividing two; its global monodromy is not required to be quadratic. The quadratic specialization is an endpoint, not the definition of the general construction. Cover root-Picard objects (L,K_R,K_R²≅L|R), the square-action quotient and gerbe, root-Picard-with-section objects, root symmetric powers and their smoothness, addition and ordered maps, the modified-unit adelic GROUPoid, invariant tensor local systems L_d, collision descent, H^d=exterior^dH1 with all other degrees zero under geometric nontriviality, high-degree Abel–Jacobi descent for d≥ρ+max(2g−1,1), independent extension to every integer Picard degree, hat-space local systems by Abel–Jacobi PULLBACK, multiplicative coherence, the ramified norm and the two-categorical exact sequence (A.11). Import Scheme and stack foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1/3) and upstream JacobianChallenge through SF.3 for generic root-stack, Picard/section and cohomology geometry; import Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5/7/8) for sheaf/descent/trace tools, and existing Mathlib exterior-power algebra. Do not place the generic nonreduced root-fibre calculation here: SF.1 supplies [SpecK[t]/t² /μ2], whose reduction alone is Bμ2. Tests: R=∅ recovers the unramified construction; a nontrivial unramified character of order three is allowed; d=0 gives the unit; exterior powers vanish above dimH1; degree-d Picard components are torsors; different auxiliary divisors give canonically identical extension; zero sections have rank-one hat stalks; root norms at R are squares of the upstairs fibre; double-coset stabilizers contribute 1/Aut. The root norm exact sequence must not be misread as injectivity of Pic groups. Resolve nonrepresentable 'finite' map conventions and all descent/coherence exercises in G4 before claiming closure. Export the character sheaf and trace/norm compatibility to ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil, not its specialized matrix stacks.

routes.title: Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves, Part II: ind-objects modulo constructibles
routes.reason: EDC.5 explicitly stops at bounded constructible perverse sheaves; Mathlib already provides Ind and abelianness, but not the paper's mc quotient interface. GS.3 needs a reusable exact categorical contract. IG.4 has a different filtered-colimit support criterion; import/reconcile rather than assert it is the same theorem.
routes.brief: Build a narrow reusable extension of Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.5), using the EXISTING Mathlib CategoryTheory.Ind, fully faithful Yoneda embedding and abelian Ind instance. First work for an essentially small finite-length abelian category C, proving that its essential image is Serre in Ind(C), then construct the exact Serre quotient Ind(C)/C with its universal property. Define mc-isomorphisms by constructible kernel/cokernel and mc-zero morphisms by constructible image, as Yun–Zhang19 Definition3.32 does after C=Perv_c(B,Qℓ). Prove the two-out-of-three/composition calculus, the ideal property of mc-zero maps, the factorization criterion, and the passage from mc-commuting squares/actions to genuine commuting squares/actions in the quotient. Supply explicit universe/skeleton choices; do not declare every ind-perverse sheaf constructible or assume the filtered colimit is a bounded constructible complex. Tests: every morphism between two constructible objects is mc-invertible in the quotient; a genuine isomorphism is mc; the identity of an infinite direct sum of nonzero skyscrapers is not mc-zero; maps factoring through one constructible object are mc-zero; two truncated degree translations differ from their composite only by a constructible image. Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.3) owns the geometric truncations, horocycle decomposition, finite core and Hecke/Satake application, and imports this formalism. Igusa varieties and torsion concentration (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.4) is a related filtered-colimit consumer, but its nearby-cycle support inequalities are not supplied by a Serre quotient and are not replanned here. No purity, arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity or compact-cohomology finiteness follows merely from this quotient construction.

review.reason: Checked on the page image. μ(c) has Σ a_i = nc, and μ_i = ±1 naturally means the coweights (1,0,…,0) and (0,…,0,−1), with type +1 meaning E_{i−1} ↪ E_i. Under that identification the printed μ′ has total degree Σμ_i + n·deg D∞ = 2n·deg D∞ ≠ 0 in general, so Sht^{μ′}_n(Σ) (with E_{r′} ≅ τE_0) is empty while Sht^μ_n(Σ;D∞) need not be (for example the Drinfeld case r = 1, μ = −1, D∞ = −(1/n)∞^(1)). The proof's own chain F_{r+1} = (τE_0)(D∞ − c^(1)y^(1)) changes degree by −nc^(1), which is type μ(−c^(1)). The paper never states the identification of ±1 with coweights, and only the unnatural choice +1 ↔ (0,…,0,−1) would make the printed sign consistent. As printed, Lemma 3.7 is false under the natural reading, and the intended statement is clear from its proof.

review.reason: The mismatch is real. When g′ = g (g = 1 and ρ = 0, or g = 0 and ρ = 2) and N ≥ 1, the printed bound of Theorem 5.6 allows 2g−1+N ≤ d ≤ 2g+N−1, where Lemma 5.19's stated hypothesis fails; yet the proof of Theorem 5.6 invokes the lemma. But the only use of 2g+N in the lemma is the Riemann–Roch count above, which needs one factor only. The finding's locator should drop Theorem 5.20 and Proposition 5.18: neither proof uses Lemma 5.19, so their printed bound d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g} is not touched by this finding. Theorem 7.4 is affected only through Theorem 5.6, so it too holds as printed. The extraction's items 118, 119, 121 and 148 should keep explicit bounds; see item 118's corrected statement.
review.originalLocator: Theorems5.6,5.20,7.4 and Lemma5.19, pp.470,487–491,510; published version
review.amendedCorrection: No strengthening of Theorems 5.6 or 7.4 is needed. The dimension count in Lemma 5.19 needs Riemann–Roch on one factor only: apply it to X^{√R}_{d+ρ−N±−1} with N± = min(N+,N−), which requires d ≥ 2g + min(N+,N−). The other factor is smooth of dimension d+ρ−N∓−1 (Lemma A.4), and the total is m−2, so dim C_d ≤ m−1. The weaker bound follows from d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g}: if N = 0 it is 2g, and if N+ ≥ 1 (resp. N− ≥ 1) then 2g′−1+N ≥ 2g−1+N ≥ 2g+N− (resp. 2g+N+). So Lemma 5.19 holds under d ≥ max{2g′−1+N, 2g+min(N+,N−)}, and Theorem 5.6 holds with its printed bound. Replace the extraction's correction, 'use max(2g′−1+N, 2g+N, 3g−2+N)'. The term 3g−2+N is in any case redundant: 3g−2 ≤ 4g−3+ρ = 2g′−1 because g = 0 forces ρ ≥ 2.

There the Frobenius isomorphism lives in Bun_T = Pic_{X′}/Pic_X and may absorb ν^*M, so only Σ_iμ_i ≡ #Σ∞ mod 2 is needed. This agrees with Definition 4.4 whenever an admissible D′∞ exists. sourceIssues.reason: Theorems 1.2–1.3 allow Σ∞ = ∅; indeed §1.2.1 says they are new 'even in the unramified case' Σ = ∅. Yet the cycles Z^{μ′} are needed for all μ′ ∈ T_{r,Σ}: Theorem 1.2 takes arbitrary μ, μ′, and Theorem 1.3's ε_{r1} involves σ_i-translates, which flip single signs by Lemma 4.10. Replace each h□_x by f□_x, which is left GL2(O_x)-invariant by Lemma 2.5, to get f^□_{Σ±}, to which Lemma 2.3 applies. By Lemma 2.6, h□_x − f□_x = φ1 + φ2 with φ1 right A(O_x)-invariant and φ2 left A(O_x)-η_x-eigen. For such φ the global distribution vanishes: J(φ⊗f′,s1,s2) = 0, by substituting h2 ↦ h2t (resp. h1 ↦ h1t) in (2.2) with t ∈ A(O_x), η_x(t) = −1, since the degree regularisation is A(O)-invariant. Each J_π(φ⊗f′) = 0 too (proof of Proposition 2.8). Hence J(f_{Σ±}) = J(f^□_{Σ±}) = Σ_π J_π(f^□_{Σ±}) = Σ_π J_π(f_{Σ±}), which is what (7.10) uses.

For zg the residues are [[0,0],[z,z]], so h̃□(zg) = (1+η̄(z))², whose average over O_x^× is 2; hence h□_x(g) = 2. For zug the residues are [[zb,zb],[z,z]], all units, so h̃□(zug) = ½(1+η̄(zb))²(1+η̄(z))² = 0 because η̄(zb) = −η̄(z); hence h□_x(ug) = 0. The proof of Theorem 2.2 uses left Iw_S-invariance to force the Eisenstein character χ to be unramified on S, so that a^S_Eis(f^S) = 0 kills the continuous part. Lemma 2.6 and Proposition 2.8 compare only the local J_{π_x}, never the global J(f) that (7.10) expands spectrally.

gates.name: Close the Hecke-domain repair
gates.remaining: Prove Theorem7.5 and the combined image-algebra/projector argument entirely for H_G^(Σ∪R). The YZ17 Lemma9.1/Theorem9.2 passages were read: choose all auxiliary places outside the additional finite set R, prove finite generation and Eisenstein support for the restricted algebra, and use strong multiplicity one there. Alternatively provide genuinely new R-local test operations. Do not silently claim the printed larger domain.
gates.resolution: E28: Theorem 7.5's Hecke-domain comparison is not established as stated. The repair through H_G^(Σ∪R) is recorded; YZ17's density and strong multiplicity one are cited suppliers.

gates.name: Complete the finite-type and high-instability branches
gates.remaining: Give the finite-type proof when r<#Σ∞ without empty K_r colimits. Construct a cofinal high-bound system whose added strata satisfy Lemma3.28, and write the kernel as well as cokernel bounds in Lemma3.37 from the long exact sequence. Distinguish V≤i (perverse-degree truncations followed by colimit) from finite geometric truncations.
gates.resolution: E10, E11 and E15 record the finite-type and high-instability gaps.

gates.name: Read and instantiate the external geometric contracts
gates.remaining: Read Lafforgue arXiv1209.5352 Proposition2.11/Lemme2.13, Varshavsky2004 Proposition2.16(a), Blum–Stuhler1997 Theorem3.1.4, and the cited YZ17 §6–7 local-model/horocycle proofs in their precise versions. The YZ17 octahedron and Frobenius-trace contracts have been read, but not their full recursive foundations. Verify every master-diagram factorization and the stronger auxiliary-level tangent argument.
gates.resolution: Lafforgue, Varshavsky, Blum–Stuhler and YZ17 are cited suppliers.

gates.name: Root-stack and character-sheaf closure
gates.remaining: Supply all AppendixA descent/coherence exercises, the exact 2-categorical meaning of (A.11), and the proper/quasifinite/tame replacement or convention for nonrepresentable maps called finite. Keep nilpotents in the zero-section fibre; prove the root norm and weighted Picard-groupoid counting under the corrected definitions.
gates.resolution: E33 records the fibre over a(x) = 0. The Appendix A descent exercises the paper leaves are routine proof work.

gates.name: Resolve low-genus largeness endpoints
gates.remaining: Check whether Theorems5.6/5.20/7.4 hold at their smaller printed thresholds in the g′=g cases. The checkpoint uses the sufficient common larger bound needed by Lemma5.19 and smallness; this suffices for the eventual Hecke comparison but is not a proof of each advertised endpoint.
gates.resolution: E20: the common larger degree bound suffices for the comparison; the printed low-genus endpoints remain unproved.

gates.name: Finish atomic coverage and proof-source closure
gates.remaining: Split the bundled generic constructions: Proposition3.9 smooth/DM/separated conclusions, Corollary3.22's four cases, master-diagram Definitions5.7–5.11, Lemmas3.24/3.37 and character-sheaf coherence; expand unnumbered local character/quotient/deformation inputs into declaration-sized contracts. validation.internal: 184 unique item IDs; every missing item routed exactly once; each definition/construction has an API outline and at least three tests; every theorem has a proof outline. These checks do not certify mathematical closure.

nonTheoremScope.statement: The tensor-factor description of π-isotypical cohomology is described as expected; it is not proved in this paper and is not included among proved target items.

The determinant/nondegeneracy assertion concerns the genuine Frobenius-q eigenspace, not an automatically semisimple generalized eigenspace. It is a conjecture, not a theorem or a proven BSD/rank-3 consequence.
Odd r is permitted here when #Σ∞ is odd. The first Yun–Zhang paper has even r; do not reuse the existing first-paper brief's r=1 test as a theorem of that unramified even-r paper.

sourceIssueScope.status: Unreviewed worker findings; no independent review object is asserted.
sourceIssueScope.caution: ‘new’ means no existing correction was located in the listed searches, not an originality claim or proof of exhaustive absence. Some findings are gaps in the printed proof with sufficient repairs, not disproofs of the main theorem.
discardedCandidates: The expected-dimension formula on p.487 ALREADY subtracts 2dim Hk_G; the initial text-reading suspicion was false and is not an issue.
Lemma5.12's norm-difference formula is a rational expression whose ramified poles cancel. It is not a twist-type error.
HbarΣ includes the Picard/Satake factor even if V is finite-dimensional, so its Krull dimension one is not contradicted by the finite-type shtuka case.
pendingChecks: Stack maps called finite in §6.1.4/A.2.1 can have stabilizer kernels; resolve the authors' convention and replace by the exact proper/quasifinite/tame cohomological contract where necessary. Not yet classified as a source error.

summaryBefore: Whole-published-paper checkpoint for the ramified, Iwahori-level two-variable higher Gross–Zagier formula. Reuse the proposed ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil extension from Yun–Zhang17 and Feng–Yun–Zhang24. Separate ramified geometric class field theory and modulo-constructible ind-perverse machinery from its cycle application. Corrected definitions retain root-stack nilpotents, determinant-zero square-root matrices, ordered configuration covers, finite-type truncation cases and every normalization factor. Main-source reading is complete; recursive source closure and final atomization remain open, so this is not a complete extraction or formalization.
